findings.question: 1. As of Sept 2026, does the latest localstack/localstack image need an auth token or account to start, or to use SQS, DynamoDB and SSM? What changed in 2025-2026? Can it run free in GitHub Actions, does that need a secret, and what is the last tag that works with no token?
findings.answer:
YES, the latest image needs a token. From release 2026.03.0 (23 March 2026), localstack/localstack and localstack/localstack-pro are the same unified image. It will not start without LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN (a developer token or a CI auth token). The auth-token docs call the token mandatory: without a valid one, license activation fails and the container exits. This applies before you touch SQS, DynamoDB or SSM. The temporary bypass LOCALSTACK_ACKNOWLEDGE_ACCOUNT_REQUIREMENT=1 stopped working on 6 April 2026.

Other changes in 2025-2026:
- The GitHub repo localstack/localstack was archived (read-only) on 23 March 2026.
- Versioning moved from semver to calver. v4.14.0 was the last semver release. Current tags are latest/stable = 2026.08.3 (pushed 16 Sep 2026), plus YYYY.MM and YYYY.MM.patch tags. The 'nightly' tag was replaced by 'dev'.
- Plans: Hobby (free, non-commercial only, about 30 services including Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB and SSM Parameter Store; no ECR, no IAM enforcement, no local persistence), Base ($39/month billed annually, $45 monthly), Ultimate ($89/month billed annually) and Enterprise. There is also a Student plan through the GitHub Student Developer Pack and free OSS/non-profit plans.
- CI credits: the first plan limited CI credits and gave the free tier none. After community pushback, LocalStack's pricing update said there are 'no more limitations on CI credits for any plan' (subject to a fair-usage policy), and 'Testing in CI' is listed for Hobby.
- Telemetry: the plans table lists 'Telemetry Sharing' as 'enforced' on Hobby, 'default on' for Base, Ultimate and Student, and 'optional' only on Enterprise. DISABLE_EVENTS=1 is the documented opt-out, but it seems not to apply on Hobby. License-activation calls to api.localstack.cloud always happen; offline activation lasts 24 hours.

GitHub Actions: the latest image can run there for free on a Hobby or Student token, but only with a secret (LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN stored as a GitHub secret). GitHub does not pass secrets to workflows triggered by pull requests from forks.

Last tag that works without a token: localstack/localstack:4.14.0 (floating tag 4.14). It was released 26 Feb 2026 for amd64 and arm64, and Docker Hub shows it has not been re-pushed since. The docs say semver was used 'through v4.14.0' and calver starts at 2026.03.0. LocalStack's own blog suggests pinning an older tag (it gives 4.12 as an example), and third-party write-ups say v4.14.0 and earlier run without a token. The cost of pinning: no security patches or bug fixes ever again. Some reports say 4.4.0 was the last community release; that is wrong, since 4.5 through 4.14 were community releases too. I did not run 4.14.0 myself, so smoke-test it before relying on it.

findings.question: 2. In the free offering, is Lambda with PackageType Image supported? Is an SQS event source mapping with FunctionResponseTypes ReportBatchItemFailures supported?
findings.answer:
Image Lambdas: NO in the free offering. In the last community code (v4.14.0), CreateFunction with PackageType=Image is accepted, but invoking the function fails. DockerRuntimeExecutor.get_image() raises NotImplementedError("Container images are a Pro feature.") when the function has no runtime, which is always the case for image functions. This gate has been in place since about v3.0.2. On the unified image, ECR is listed only for Base and Ultimate, not Hobby. The Lambda docs and the licensing page do not say explicitly whether image functions work on Hobby, but Hobby is described as equivalent to the old community image, so expect no.

SQS event source mapping with ReportBatchItemFailures: YES, for zip functions. The Lambda docs' coverage table shows 'FunctionResponseTypes - Enabling ReportBatchItemFailures' as fully implemented for SQS. The v4.14.0 source (event_source_mapping/pollers/sqs_poller.py) catches PartialBatchFailureError, parses batchItemFailures, and deletes only the successful message IDs. Failed messages become visible again through the normal visibility timeout (this code does not reset visibility), so a worker's own ChangeMessageVisibility is respected.

What this means for Relay: both Lambdas ship as container images, so neither free LocalStack option (4.14.0 or Hobby) can run the real SQS-to-worker path. Moto can't either: its docs say 'Invoking a Function with PackageType=Image is not yet supported'. Floci claims both image Lambdas and ReportBatchItemFailures, but it is young (see finding 7). The practical fix is a small local stand-in for the event source mapping that polls SQS and invokes the worker image's built-in Runtime Interface Emulator (RIE).

findings.question: 3. Does LocalStack DynamoDB support TransactWriteItems with per-item ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure=ALL_OLD, returning the old Item inside CancellationReasons?
findings.answer:
UNVERIFIED, and I found no primary source either way. LocalStack's DynamoDB is a proxy in front of AWS's DynamoDB Local. In v4.14.0, provider.transact_write_items just calls forward_request, with no special handling for TransactionCanceledException, CancellationReasons or ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure. DynamoDB Local has been bundled in the image since LocalStack 2.1.0, and the download URL it uses is 'dynamodb_local_latest.zip'. So the behaviour is whatever the bundled DynamoDB Local does.

DynamoDB Local added 'support for ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure' in 2.2.0 and 1.25.0 (December 2023), and in embedded mode in 2.4.0 and 2.5.0. Neither the release notes nor the announcement say whether that covers the per-item parameter inside TransactWriteItems, i.e. whether CancellationReasons[i].Item gets filled in.

LocalStack issue #9040 (Aug 2023, 'implement ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure') says the Item was missing. It was closed only when the repo was archived, with no resolution recorded. LocalStack's own parity tests and snapshots for v4.14.0 have no test covering CancellationReasons or ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure.

Two related facts: botocore does expose e.response['CancellationReasons'] for Python (boto3 #2657 shows the raw payload with Code, Item and Message). And DynamoDB Local never throws TransactionConflictException.

Recommendation: don't make Relay's correctness depend on this field. Treat both duplicate and stale as 'ack and drop'. If you want the duplicate-vs-stale distinction for metrics, fall back to a consistent GetItem when Item is missing.

findings.question: 4. Does LocalStack SQS implement RedrivePolicy maxReceiveCount (moving to a DLQ), ChangeMessageVisibility and message attributes faithfully?
findings.answer:
YES, all three. LocalStack uses its own Python SQS provider, available on Hobby, Base and Ultimate, and in 4.14.0.
- DLQ: in the v4.14.0 source (services/sqs/models.py), StandardQueue.receive() and FifoQueue.receive() increment receive_count and then move the message to the DLQ when `message.receive_count > max_receive_count`. That matches AWS: the message moves on the receive attempt after maxReceiveCount deliveries.
- ChangeMessageVisibility: update_visibility_timeout() is implemented. VisibilityTimeout=0 removes the message from in-flight and requeues it immediately.
- Message attributes: returned with MD5OfMessageAttributes recomputed.
- Also supported: message move tasks (StartMessageMoveTask) and the /_aws/sqs developer endpoint for peeking at messages without side effects.

Documented gaps:
- Changing MessageRetentionPeriod doesn't affect existing messages.
- Retention isn't enforced unless SQS_ENABLE_MESSAGE_RETENTION_PERIOD=1.
- The queue URL format depends on SQS_ENDPOINT_STRATEGY ('standard' is recommended).

findings.question: 5. moto server mode (motoserver/moto): SQS RedrivePolicy/DLQ moves, ChangeMessageVisibility, DynamoDB TransactWriteItems with CancellationReasons and ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure, SSM GetParameter/PutParameter incl. SecureString? Token needed? Latest tag?
findings.answer:
Moto covers everything Relay's local tests need. It is Apache-2.0 licensed, needs no account, token or telemetry opt-out, and accepts dummy credentials. It serves all services on port 5000 (change with MOTO_PORT). POST /moto-api/reset wipes state between tests, and a dashboard is at /moto-api/.

Latest image: motoserver/moto:5.2.3 (the same image as :latest). It was pushed 22 Aug 2026 for amd64 and arm64. The CHANGELOG gives its digest as sha256:91fd602a21f49cf9eb82fdf474015a3c131d40104c8297ea6a2ca920708ae32c. Earlier releases: 5.2.2 (6 Jun 2026), 5.2.1 and 5.2.0 (May 2026). 5.2.0 dropped Python 3.9 and added 'ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure for all operations'.

SQS:
- change_message_visibility and change_message_visibility_batch are implemented, as are list_dead_letter_source_queues and set_queue_attributes.
- DLQ moves: in receive_message, a visible message goes to the DLQ when `message.approximate_receive_count >= redrive_policy['maxReceiveCount']`. That check runs before mark_received increments the count, so the move happens on the receive attempt after maxReceiveCount deliveries, which matches AWS.
- ChangeMessageVisibility validates the receipt handle (ReceiptHandleIsInvalid) and enforces the 12-hour cap. VisibilityTimeout=0 makes the message visible again.
- Message attributes and MessageAttributeNames patterns are supported (the patterns were extended in 5.2.0).
- Not implemented: start_message_move_task, list_message_move_tasks and cancel_message_move_task. relayctl's redrive should therefore do receive, send to the main queue and delete from the DLQ, rather than use StartMessageMoveTask; or feature-detect it.

DynamoDB: transact_write_items is implemented. It reads each op's ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure, and on a failed condition with ALL_OLD it attaches current.to_json()['Attributes']. TransactionCanceledException then builds CancellationReasons as {Code, Message} plus 'Item' when present, and {Code:'None'} for items that succeeded. The state is rolled back. The Item-in-CancellationReasons fix came from moto issue #5204 / PR #5482 (2022).

SSM: get_parameter, put_parameter and get_parameters_by_path are implemented. SecureString defaults to KeyId alias/aws/ssm. The stored value is the fake string 'kms:<keyid>:<plaintext>'. With WithDecryption=True you get the plaintext; with False you get the 'kms:...' string, not real ciphertext, so tests should not assert on the encrypted form.

Not covered: invoking PackageType=Image Lambdas, and SQS event source mappings for image Lambdas.

findings.question: 6. Alternatives: amazon/dynamodb-local + softwaremill/elasticmq-native. Feature gaps for the above?
findings.answer:
amazon/dynamodb-local: the latest tag is 3.3.1 (= :latest), pushed 31 Jul 2026 for amd64 and arm64. The release notes date it 28 May 2026: PartiQL deps, AWS SDK for Java 2.48.3, CVE fixes. Earlier: 3.3.0 (Jan 2026, multi-attribute GSI keys), 3.2.0, 3.1.0, 3.0.0 (moved to AWS SDK for Java v2).
- It is AWS's own engine, so it is the most trustworthy check of condition-expression and transaction semantics. It also runs underneath LocalStack.
- Gaps: it never throws TransactionConflictException, doesn't support tagging or PITR, and treats table names as case-insensitive. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID must be letters and digits only ('test' works).
- Per-item ALL_OLD inside TransactWriteItems is not documented either way (see Q3).
- It sends telemetry by default since 2.1.0; turn it off with -disableTelemetry.
- It has no SQS and no SSM.

softwaremill/elasticmq-native: the latest tag is 1.7.1 (= :latest), pushed 5 Apr 2026. 1.7.0 came out 4 Apr 2026 with a new UI; 1.6.16 (Feb 2026) handles JSON-protocol errors, which boto3 and aws-sdk-go-v2 need. The SQS API is on port 9324 and the UI image is separate.
- It supports DLQs with maxReceiveCount (documented in the config file as deadLettersQueue { name, maxReceiveCount }), ChangeMessageVisibility, message attributes, FIFO, and fair-queue MessageGroupId (1.6.14). Message move tasks were implemented via issue #858 / PR #987; I could not confirm which release.
- Gaps and risks: RedrivePolicy set through the CreateQueue/SetQueueAttributes API has older open issues saying the DLQ link was silently not created (#124, open since 2018). It is probably fixed, since later issues argue about the maxReceiveCount format, but it is unconfirmed. Queue-URL host config (node-address) needs care inside compose. And it has no SSM.

Overall: this pair still needs a third emulator for SSM (the watermark, chaos flags and Salesforce credentials all live there), so in practice that means moto anyway. It adds containers without closing the image-Lambda / event-source-mapping gap. The one real benefit is DynamoDB Local as a cross-check of DynamoDB behaviour.

findings.question: 7. (Extra) Are there new no-token LocalStack replacements that emulate image Lambdas plus the SQS event source mapping?
findings.answer:
Floci (github.com/floci-io/floci) is MIT licensed and needs no account or token. It launched around 22 March 2026, is written in Java/Quarkus, and listens on port 4566. Image: floci/floci. The latest numbered release is 2.1.0 (15 Sep 2026), with variants 2.1.0-compat (adds the AWS CLI and boto3), -baseline and -cedar; nightlies are published every day.

Its docs claim:
- Lambda with PackageType Image, from emulated ECR or local Docker images; needs /var/run/docker.sock mounted.
- SQS event source mappings that honour ReportBatchItemFailures.
- SQS DLQs.
- SSM SecureString.
- A native DynamoDB with transactions.

It is very immature for Relay's needs, though:
- TransactWriteItems was not atomic (failed transactions left partial writes) until PR #3189, merged 7 Sep 2026 and first shipped in 2.1.0.
- Composite keys containing '#' could collide and overwrite each other (issue #3800, opened 17 Sep 2026). The fix landed after 2.1.0, so the latest numbered release still has it, and Relay's single-table keys will likely use '#'.
- The SQS event source mapping deleted messages on malformed partial-batch responses (issue #3152, fixed after 2.0.1).
- I found no documentation of CancellationReasons Item support.

Worth re-evaluating later, but don't base Relay's failure-injection proofs on it today. LocalEmu (a pip-installed emulator) also appeared in search results; I did not evaluate it.

findings.question: 8. (Extra) How should the local stand-in for the SQS-to-Lambda event source mapping behave, and how do SDKs get pointed at the emulator without code changes?

recommendations: Stop using localstack/localstack:latest in Relay. Since 2026.03.0 it won't start without LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN, which means a GitHub secret, no runs on pull requests from forks, and Hobby's non-commercial terms with telemetry you can't turn off. That breaks the plan's rule that CI runs end to end without credentials. Update PLAN.md: the 'localstack | localstack/localstack' row in the Local stack table, the '1.1 Setup' deliverable, and the CI and resume wording ('LocalStack integration').

Make motoserver/moto:5.2.3 the single AWS emulator for SQS, DynamoDB and SSM. Optionally pin the digest: motoserver/moto:5.2.3@sha256:91fd602a21f49cf9eb82fdf474015a3c131d40104c8297ea6a2ca920708ae32c. Expose port 5000, add a healthcheck on /moto-api/, and call POST http://moto:5000/moto-api/reset between integration tests. Moto's source shows it supports RedrivePolicy DLQ moves with AWS-like timing, ChangeMessageVisibility, message attributes, TransactWriteItems with CancellationReasons[].Item on ALL_OLD, and SSM SecureString, with no token or account.

Add a small 'esm-pump' service (about 80-100 lines of Python) that stands in for the SQS event source mapping. It receives up to 10 messages with AttributeNames/MessageSystemAttributeNames=All and MessageAttributeNames=All, builds Lambda-shaped SQS records, POSTs them to the worker image's RIE at http://worker:8080/2015-03-31/functions/function/invocations, applies AWS's batchItemFailures rules (invalid JSON, empty or unknown itemIdentifier, or an exception means the whole batch failed), and DeleteMessageBatch-es only the successes. This is necessary: no free emulator except the immature Floci can invoke PackageType=Image Lambdas. The real event source mapping then gets covered by the post-deploy smoke test.

Use this docker-compose set: aws = motoserver/moto:5.2.3. fake-salesforce = your own Python stub. worker and reconciler = built FROM public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:<your 3.x>. ingest = built FROM public.ecr.aws/lambda/provided:al2023. esm-pump = your own. Give every app container AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://aws:5000, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=test, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=test and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1. Both boto3 and aws-sdk-go-v2 honour AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, so no code needs an endpoint parameter. Pin the Lambda base images by digest in the Dockerfiles.

Optional DynamoDB parity check: add amazon/dynamodb-local:3.3.1 under a compose profile (e.g. 'parity') with command '-jar DynamoDBLocal.jar -inMemory -sharedDb -disableTelemetry'. Run only the conditional-write and transaction tests with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_DYNAMODB=http://dynamodb:8000. It is AWS's own engine, so if moto and DynamoDB Local disagree, investigate before trusting either.

Don't make the worker's correctness depend on CancellationReasons[].Item. Duplicate and stale both mean 'ack and drop'. If you want separate duplicate/stale metrics, read Item when it is present and otherwise fall back to a ConsistentRead GetItem. Support for Item in LocalStack and DynamoDB Local is unverified.

For relayctl's DLQ redrive, do receive, send to the main queue, then delete from the DLQ, rather than StartMessageMoveTask: moto doesn't implement message move tasks, while AWS and LocalStack do. Tests also shouldn't assert on the encrypted form of SSM SecureString values (moto returns 'kms:alias/aws/ssm:<plaintext>' when WithDecryption=False).

CI safety guard: the integration job gets no AWS credentials other than the dummy 'test' values, and it fails fast if AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is unset, so a test can never reach real AWS. OIDC role assumption belongs only in the main-branch deploy job.

Fallback if you want to stay on LocalStack without a token: pin localstack/localstack:4.14.0 (released 26 Feb 2026, the last semver release, no token needed) and set DISABLE_EVENTS=1. Its SQS behaviour is faithful, but it is frozen with no security patches, and it still can't invoke image Lambdas ('Container images are a Pro feature'), so you'd need the esm-pump anyway. Smoke-test that it starts in CI before relying on it.

Watch Floci (floci/floci, latest 2.1.0, 15 Sep 2026, MIT, no token), but don't adopt it yet. It is the only free emulator claiming image Lambdas plus ReportBatchItemFailures, but TransactWriteItems wasn't atomic until 2.1.0, and a '#' composite-key collision bug is fixed only after 2.1.0. Both are the exact behaviours Relay's tests are meant to prove.
All tag dates above come from the Docker Hub API as of 2026-09-22. Re-check them when you write the compose file, and record the exact tags and digests in the README so the results can be reproduced.

findings.question: 1. Developer Edition signup (Sept 2026): URL, naming, inactivity expiry, email verification and MFA
findings.answer:
URL: https://developer.salesforce.com/signup. Older links point to https://www.salesforce.com/form/developer-signup/. I couldn't fetch either page (403 or error), so the form fields below come from third-party guides. Salesforce's own name is still 'Salesforce Developer Edition'. Since March 2025 new signups get the 'new Developer Edition, now with Agentforce and Data Cloud', which blogs and courses call the 'Agentforce Developer Edition'. The older kind is now labelled 'Developer Edition (Legacy)'. In April 2026 (TDX) Salesforce added the Agentforce Vibes IDE, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and hosted MCP servers. None of this changes the REST or OAuth basics.

Form: First name, Last name, Email (must be a real inbox you can open), Role/Job title, Company, Country, Postal code, and Username. The username must be email-shaped and unique across all Salesforce orgs, but it does not have to be a real mailbox, e.g. yourname.relay@example.dev. Accept the terms and click 'Sign Me Up'. You get a 'Welcome to Salesforce: Verify your account' email (sender developer@salesforce.com). Click 'Verify Account', then set a password (at least 8 characters with a letter and a number) and a security question.

Expiry, the key risk: a new Developer Edition org that nobody logs into for 45 days is DELETED IMMEDIATELY. Legacy DE orgs are queued for deletion after 180 days. Salesforce sends a warning email first. Bob Buzzard reports that just authenticating was not enough to reset the timer; the org needed real activity. It is unverified whether logins by the client-credentials integration count. So log into the UI and click around at least every 30 days, and keep a seed script so sample data can be recreated.

MFA and verification: the phishing-resistant MFA enforcement (July to Sept 2026) covers only paid production and sandbox orgs. Developer Edition, trial and scratch orgs are exempt. Standard identity checks still apply: expect an emailed verification code on first login from a new browser, and you may be asked to register Salesforce Authenticator or a TOTP app. Your My Domain is generated for you, in the form https://<something>-dev-ed.develop.my.salesforce.com (observed as orgfarm-<hex>-dev-ed.develop.my.salesforce.com). One unconfirmed source says My Domain cannot be renamed in DE orgs.

findings.question: 2. Is creating NEW connected apps restricted in favour of External Client Apps (ECAs)? What is the setting, can it be re-enabled, and does it apply to new DE orgs?
findings.answer:
Yes. Salesforce knowledge article 005228017, 'New Connected Apps Can No Longer Be Created in Spring '26', says creating connected apps in the UI is disabled by default on all new orgs. From Spring '26 customers can't turn it back on themselves; they must ask Salesforce Support. Creation is blocked through both the UI and the API; the only exception is installing a package. Salesforce also says Support will stop granting this in a future release.

The setting is 'Allow creation of connected apps', at Setup > Apps > External Client Apps > Settings. In orgs created in Summer '25 or Winter '26 the toggle is still visible. In Spring '26 and later orgs it is gone or cannot be switched on.

Timeline (secondary sources): Winter '26 (Oct 2025) turned it off for newly provisioned orgs, and Spring '26 (early 2026) turned it off for all orgs. A new DE org signed up in Sept 2026 counts as a new org, and DE orgs have no standard Support case access. In practice you cannot create a connected app, and 'New Connected App' in App Manager is greyed out or missing.

An External Client App (ECA) is the right choice. ECAs support the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow; they do not support the username-password flow. Existing connected apps keep working. Other dates reported: the device flow is limited to ECAs from 30 Nov 2026, and a 'migrate all connected apps to ECAs' milestone is reported for Summer '27.

findings.question: 3. Exact current Setup steps to create an External Client App for the client credentials flow
findings.answer:
Required permission: 'Create, edit, and delete External Client Apps'. The DE admin has it.

A) Create the app. Gear icon > Setup > Quick Find 'External Client App Manager' > 'New External Client App'. The same button is also in Setup > App Manager.
Basic Information:
- External Client App Name (e.g. Relay Integration)
- API Name (auto-filled; letters, digits and underscores only)
- Contact Email: use the org's email address, because the verification code for viewing the secret is sent there
- Distribution State = Local

B) Expand 'API (Enable OAuth Settings)' and tick 'Enable OAuth'.
- Callback URL: the field is there and the form may require it (multiple URLs go on separate lines, 2,000-character limit), but client credentials never uses it. Put in a placeholder such as https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/callback or http://localhost:1717/OauthRedirect.
- OAuth Scopes: move 'Manage user data via APIs (api)' to Selected. Don't rely on 'full', 'web' or 'refresh_token, offline_access': the client credentials flow filters those out automatically.
- Under Flow Enablement, tick 'Enable Client Credentials Flow' and accept the security warning if one appears.
- Security section: leave the defaults. These are 'Require secret for Web Server Flow', 'Require secret for Refresh Token Flow' and 'Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension for Supported Authorization Flows'; they don't affect client credentials.
- Click Create.

C) Set the Run As (execution) user. This is a separate step and the most common failure. Open the app in External Client App Manager, go to the Policies tab and click Edit (or pick 'Edit Policies' from the row's dropdown). Under OAuth Policies > 'OAuth Flows and External Client App Enhancements', tick 'Enable Client Credentials Flow' and put the username (not the email) in 'Run As (Username)'. Save. If you skip this, token requests fail with 'invalid_grant: no client credentials user enabled'.

Which user: the simplest choice is your admin username. The better practice is a dedicated user with the 'Salesforce Integration' license, the 'Minimum Access - API Only Integrations' profile, and a permission set granting Read on Account and Opportunity. One secondary source says DE includes one Salesforce Integration license; Salesforce's page doesn't give a DE number.

Permitted Users: Salesforce's connected-app docs say 'All users may self-authorize' and 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized' don't apply to the execution user. Leave the default. Some vendor guides switch to 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized' and add the System Administrator profile; do that only if you hit authorization errors. IP Relaxation can stay at the default in DE, because the admin profile has no login IP ranges by default.

Token lifetime: set it on the same Policies tab under Session Policies > Timeout Value (optional, see Q4).

D) Get the key and secret. Open the app > Settings tab > expand 'OAuth Settings' > 'Consumer Key and Secret'. Salesforce emails a verification code; enter it, then copy both values. On connected apps the page stays visible for about 5 minutes before asking again. If the button is missing, the user lacks the 'View All External Client Apps, view their settings, and edit their policies' permission.

E) Propagation: new apps and credential changes take up to about 10 minutes to become usable. Secondary sources say 10 to 15 minutes; I found no primary number for ECAs. Until then the token call may return invalid_client or invalid_client_id.

findings.question: 4. Token request: endpoint, body, response fields, refresh token, lifetime
findings.answer:
Endpoint: you MUST use My Domain. Salesforce's doc says: 'For this flow, requests to https://login.salesforce.com and https://test.salesforce.com aren't supported. Use your My Domain URL instead.'
Token URL: POST https://<MyDomain>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token. For DE that is https://<name>-dev-ed.develop.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token.

Request: Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with body grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<consumer key>&client_secret=<consumer secret>. You can instead send the key and secret in an HTTP Basic Authorization header (base64 of client_id:client_secret) with grant_type in the body. Never put the secret in the URL query string. Don't send a scope parameter: 'Salesforce doesn't support scopes on the token endpoint'. Scopes come from the app.

Response (Salesforce's example):
{"access_token":"...","instance_url":"https://yourInstance.salesforce.com","id":"https://login.salesforce.com/id/<OrgId>/<UserId>","token_type":"Bearer","scope":"id api","issued_at":"1657741493799","signature":"c2lnbmF0dXJl"}
Notes on the fields:
- issued_at is epoch milliseconds, as a string.
- signature is a base64 HMAC-SHA256 signed with client_secret.
- The id URL uses login.salesforce.com even though you must call My Domain.
- instance_url should be your My Domain URL; use it as the base for REST calls.
- There is NO expires_in field.
- NO refresh token: 'This flow doesn't support refresh tokens.' When the token expires, just request a new one.
- Ignore unknown fields in the parser.

Lifetime: the token is a session. Its timeout comes from the first of these that is set: the app's Session Policies 'Timeout Value', then the Run As user's profile session timeout, then the org's Session Settings timeout. The default is usually 2 hours. Because there is no expires_in, cache the token (in the Lambda's memory for warm starts), and on HTTP 401 with errorCode INVALID_SESSION_ID get a new token and retry once. Salesforce can rate-limit bursts of token requests, so don't request a token on every poll.

Useful errors:
- 'invalid_grant' / 'no client credentials user enabled': Run As is missing.
- 'invalid_client_id' or 'invalid_client': wrong key or secret, or still propagating.
- Failure against login.salesforce.com: wrong host.

Aside: AWS Secrets Manager now has managed rotation for Salesforce ECA client secrets (secret type SalesforceClientSecret, API v65.0 or later). It's optional and beyond the SSM plan.

findings.question: 5. Current REST API version (Sept 2026), release-to-version map, how to list versions
findings.answer:
Release to version:
- Winter '26 = v65.0
- Spring '26 = v66.0
- Summer '26 = v67.0
- Winter '27 = v68.0

Winter '27 went to preview sandboxes on Aug 28-29, 2026. Production instances, where DE orgs live, upgrade on Oct 3 and Oct 9-10, 2026 (UTC). So on 22 Sept 2026 a new DE org is most likely on Summer '26 (v67.0) and moves to v68.0 around 10 Oct 2026. Salesforce's REST API Developer Guide PDF is already labelled 'Version 68.0, Winter '27'.

To list versions: GET https://<MyDomain>/services/data/ returns a JSON array of {"label":"Summer '26","url":"/services/data/v67.0","version":"67.0"}. It needs no authentication and doesn't count against API limits.

Winter '27 adds a 'latest' alias (/services/data/latest/...), valid only on v68.0 and later. Sources disagree on whether it's GA or beta and whether it's available in production. Don't rely on it; pin a number.

Recommendation: pin v66.0 or v67.0 in config, e.g. SF_API_VERSION=66.0. That works both before and after the Winter '27 upgrade, and pinned versions stay supported for years; the current retirements only affect v21.0-40.0.

findings.question: 6. SOQL datetime literals, SystemModstamp precision, and the exact JSON shape of /query with Account.Name
findings.answer:
Literals: documented formats are YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ (preferred), YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+hh:mm and YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss-hh:mm. They are NOT quoted: WHERE SystemModstamp >= 2026-09-22T10:15:30Z. Quoting gives "value of filter criterion for field 'SystemModstamp' must be of type dateTime and should not be enclosed in quotes". Fractional seconds (.000Z) are reported to work but aren't in the documented list, so emit whole seconds with Z. If you ever use a +hh:mm offset in the q= parameter, the '+' must be URL-encoded as %2B, or it turns into a space. Using Z avoids that.

Precision: Salesforce DateTime fields store whole seconds. The API returns them with a .000 millisecond part and an offset with NO colon, e.g. "SystemModstamp": "2023-07-11T11:07:16.000+0000" (verbatim from an Airbyte bug report). Go's time.RFC3339 will NOT parse '+0000'; use the layout "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000-0700". Before putting a returned value back into SOQL, reformat it to ...Z.

Commit lag: SystemModstamp can be set before the transaction commits. Airbyte says a record may have its SystemModStamp set while the transaction isn't committed yet, and uses a default 10-minute lookback window to catch these.

Response shape: GET /services/data/v66.0/query?q=SELECT+Id,Name,Amount,AccountId,Account.Name,SystemModstamp+FROM+Opportunity...
{"totalSize":3,"done":true,"records":[{"attributes":{"type":"Opportunity","url":"/services/data/v66.0/sobjects/Opportunity/006..."},"Id":"006...","Name":"Acme deal","Amount":12000.0,"AccountId":"001...","Account":{"attributes":{"type":"Account","url":"/services/data/v66.0/sobjects/Account/001..."},"Name":"Acme"},"SystemModstamp":"2026-09-22T10:15:30.000+0000"}, {... "Amount":null, "AccountId":null, "Account":null ...}]}
- totalSize is the total number of matches across all pages.
- When done is false, a "nextRecordsUrl":"/services/data/v66.0/query/01g...-2000" key appears; GET it with the same Bearer token. It is absent when done is true.
- A record with an empty AccountId normally comes back as "Account": null. One R client (salesforcer) says REST may leave the relationship out entirely, so treat a missing key the same as null.
- Empty Amount is null.
- CloseDate is a date string with no time, e.g. "2026-09-22".

Batch size: the default and maximum is 2,000 records per page; the minimum is 200. You can change it with the header 'Sforce-Query-Options: batchSize=N', but the requested size isn't guaranteed. Each page (each nextRecordsUrl fetch) is one API call.

findings.question: 7. Developer Edition daily API limit; does the OAuth token endpoint count?
findings.answer:
Developer Edition gets 15,000 API requests per org per rolling 24 hours (Salesforce knowledge article 000389027). DE orgs cannot go over it; the soft-overage allowance excludes trials, DE and sandboxes. The calls that count are REST, SOAP, Bulk/Bulk 2.0 and most Connect REST calls. Every query page and every nextRecordsUrl fetch counts. GET /services/data/ (the versions list) does not.

The OAuth token endpoint (/services/oauth2/token) is not one of the listed APIs. One secondary source says token requests don't use API quota, but I found no primary Salesforce statement, so treat it as likely rather than guaranteed. Salesforce can still rate-limit bursts of token requests, so cache the token.

To check usage, every REST response carries the header 'Sforce-Limit-Info: api-usage=NN/15000', and GET /services/data/vXX.X/limits returns DailyApiRequests.

Budget: polling once a minute is about 1,440 calls a day, plus the reconciler and CLI. That fits easily; a 15-second poll (5,760 a day) still fits.

findings.question: 8. Does every Opportunity edit bump SystemModstamp? Is IsWon = true better than StageName = 'Closed Won'? Can a Closed Won Opportunity have no Amount and no Account?
findings.answer:
SystemModstamp changes on every save by a user or by an automated or system process. It changes even in cases where LastModifiedDate doesn't: a picklist value renamed by Salesforce, LastActivityDate updated by the system, roll-up summary recalculation, archive-date changes. So a new SystemModstamp does NOT mean the business fields changed. Adding a product, for example, recalculates Amount and bumps the stamp. Two saves in the same second produce the SAME SystemModstamp, because precision is one second.

IsWon vs StageName: IsWon ('Won') is read-only and set by Salesforce. It is true when the stage's Type is 'Closed/Won'. Filtering on StageName = 'Closed Won' breaks if an admin renames or translates that stage, or adds a second won stage (e.g. 'Closed Won - Renewal'). WHERE IsWon = true is more robust. IsClosed covers both won and lost.

No Amount: yes. Amount is optional; only custom validation rules would block it. If the Opportunity has products, Amount is the sum of the product lines and can't be edited.

No Account: at the API level, yes. AccountId is nullable and a community Forum Ambassador confirms 'Account is not a required field by default'. However, Salesforce's own Opportunity Fields help page labels Account Name 'Required'. So if the UI form insists on it in your org, either untick Required on the page layout (Setup > Object Manager > Opportunity > Page Layouts) or create that record through the REST API with no AccountId.

Other behaviour: Name, Stage and Close Date are required. When an open Opportunity with a future Close Date is set to Closed Won, Salesforce changes Close Date to today's UTC date, and Probability goes to 100%.

findings.question: Step-by-step student checklist for the current UI (Sept 2026)
findings.answer:
1. Go to https://developer.salesforce.com/signup. Fill in First name, Last name, a real Email, Role, Company, Country, Postal code, and a unique email-shaped Username (e.g. yourname.relay@example.dev). Accept the terms and click Sign Me Up.
2. Open the 'Verify your account' email, click Verify Account, and set a password and security question. Save your username. Expect an emailed code at your first login from a new browser.
3. Set a calendar reminder: log into the UI at least every 30 days. The org is deleted after 45 days with no login.
4. Setup > Quick Find 'My Domain'. Copy 'Current My Domain URL', e.g. https://xxxx-dev-ed.develop.my.salesforce.com.
5. Setup > Quick Find 'External Client App Manager' > New External Client App. Enter Name 'Relay Integration', API Name Relay_Integration, Contact Email = your org email, Distribution State = Local.
6. Expand API (Enable OAuth Settings) and tick Enable OAuth. Callback URL: https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/callback (placeholder). Scopes: add 'Manage user data via APIs (api)'. Flow Enablement: tick 'Enable Client Credentials Flow' and accept the warning. Leave the Security defaults. Click Create.
7. In the app, go to Policies tab > Edit > OAuth Policies > 'OAuth Flows and External Client App Enhancements'. Tick 'Enable Client Credentials Flow' and set 'Run As (Username)' to your admin username (the one from step 1). Leave Permitted Users at the default. Save.
8. Settings tab > OAuth Settings > 'Consumer Key and Secret'. Enter the emailed code and copy both values into a password manager. Never paste them into git or chat.
9. Wait about 10 minutes, then run (Windows: use curl.exe, not the PowerShell 'curl' alias):
curl.exe -s -X POST "<MY_DOMAIN_URL>/services/oauth2/token" -d "grant_type=client_credentials" --data-urlencode "client_id=<KEY>" --data-urlencode "client_secret=<SECRET>"
You should get JSON with access_token and instance_url.
10. Run: curl.exe -s "<MY_DOMAIN_URL>/services/data/" and confirm v66.0 or v67.0 is listed.
11. Create Accounts through App Launcher > Accounts > New: 'Acme Corp', 'Globex', 'Initech'.
12. Create Opportunities through App Launcher > Opportunities > New (Name, Close Date and Stage are required):
(a) 'Acme - Won', Acme, Amount 12000, Stage Closed Won.
(b) 'Initech - No Amount', Initech, Amount blank, Closed Won.
(c) 'Globex - Edited Twice', Globex, Amount 8000, Closed Won. Then edit it to Amount 8500 and save. Wait at least 2 seconds, edit Description and save again.
(d) 'Orphan - No Account', Account blank, Amount 3000, Closed Won. If the form requires Account, untick Required on the page layout or create it through the API.
(e) 'Globex - Open', Stage Prospecting. This one must NOT sync.
(f) 'Acme - Lost', Stage Closed Lost. This one must NOT sync.
Optional: 'Acme - Reverted', Closed Won and then back to Negotiation/Review, to test drift.
13. Test query:
curl.exe -s -G "<MY_DOMAIN_URL>/services/data/v66.0/query" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" --data-urlencode "q=SELECT Id, Name, Amount, StageName, IsWon, CloseDate, AccountId, Account.Name, SystemModstamp FROM Opportunity WHERE IsWon = true AND SystemModstamp >= 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z ORDER BY SystemModstamp ASC, Id ASC"
Expect records (a), (b), (c) and (d). (b) has "Amount": null and (d) has "Account": null.
14. Put these in .env (gitignored):
SF_MY_DOMAIN_URL=https://xxxx-dev-ed.develop.my.salesforce.com
SF_CLIENT_ID=<consumer key>
SF_CLIENT_SECRET=<consumer secret>
SF_API_VERSION=66.0
Optional: SF_TOKEN_URL=${SF_MY_DOMAIN_URL}/services/oauth2/token.
No username, password or security token is needed. The Run As user lives in Salesforce, not in .env.

recommendations: Change PLAN.md line 41 and Phase 1.1 from 'connected app' to 'External Client App (ECA), Distribution State Local'. New connected apps can't be created in a Sept 2026 DE org.
Change the poll filter in PLAN.md step 1 from StageName = 'Closed Won' to IsWon = true. Use the same filter in the fake Salesforce stub and the nightly reconciler.

Poll with a lookback window: query SystemModstamp >= (watermark - 10 min), ORDER BY SystemModstamp, Id. Salesforce can set SystemModstamp before the transaction commits (Airbyte defaults to a 10-minute lookback). This is safe because the consumer is already idempotent.

Treat the event key OpportunityId:SystemModstamp as a version, not a business change. System processes bump SystemModstamp, and two edits in the same second share one stamp. Make order/invoice creation idempotent on OpportunityId. If a payload arrives with the same stamp but different fields, handle it deliberately (e.g. content hash), not as a duplicate.

Parse Salesforce datetimes as '2006-01-02T15:04:05.000-0700' in Go (time.RFC3339 fails on '+0000'). Write SOQL literals as unquoted 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' so no '+' needs URL-encoding. Make the stub return exactly this format so the bug shows up locally.

Make the fake Salesforce stub match the real shapes: {totalSize, done, records[], nextRecordsUrl only when done=false}, per-record 'attributes', nested 'Account' object or null, 'Amount': null, date-only CloseDate, and a token response with no expires_in and no refresh_token.

Token client: POST to the My Domain /services/oauth2/token (never login.salesforce.com). Cache the token in the warm Lambda. On 401 INVALID_SESSION_ID, get a new token and retry once. Don't send scope. Store client_id and client_secret as SecureString in SSM.
Pin SF_API_VERSION=66.0 (or 67.0). DE instances move to Winter '27 / v68.0 around 3-10 Oct 2026, and the 'latest' alias isn't reliable.

Put the 45-day DE inactivity deletion in the manual checklist and README: log into the UI at least every 30 days, and keep the sample data reproducible (a checklist or a small REST seed script) in case the org is lost.
Log the Sforce-Limit-Info api-usage header from each poll so the 15,000/day DE limit shows up in CloudWatch.

Mark as unverified until tested in the real org: whether the ECA form requires a Callback URL, the exact propagation delay (about 10 min), whether 'Account' is left out or returned as null when empty, and whether token requests count toward API usage.

findings.question: Q1a. AWS Free Tier for accounts created after 15 July 2025: Free plan vs Paid plan, credits, the 6-month limit and what happens at the end
findings.answer:
You choose a plan at sign-up. Both plans get USD $100 in sign-up credit, plus up to another $100 for completing 'Explore AWS' activities ($20 each: EC2, RDS, Lambda, Bedrock, and 'Set up a cost budget using AWS Budgets'). So creating the $1 budget from that widget earns $20. Credits expire 12 months after the account is created.

FREE PLAN
- You are never charged.
- Only 'Always Free' offers apply. There are no short-term trials, and the legacy 12-month offers are not available to new accounts.
- The plan ends after 6 months or when the credits run out, whichever comes first. At that point 'your account closes automatically, and you lose access to your resources and data'. AWS keeps your content for 90 days. You can reopen the account by upgrading to the Paid plan within those 90 days.
- AWS emails you when 50%, 25% and 10% of credits remain, and 15, 7 and 2 days before the 6 months end.
- The account upgrades itself to Paid if you join AWS Organizations, set up a Control Tower landing zone, join the AWS Partner Network (APN), sign an Enterprise Agreement or Professional Services contract, buy a Skill Builder Team subscription, or designate the account HIPAA/SEC.
- An upgrade cannot be reversed. The console path is Upgrade plan > Upgrade account.

PAID PLAN
- You get all services and short-term trials.
- You pay normal rates for usage beyond the credits.
- The account does not close when the credits run out.

IMPLICATION FOR RELAY: a Free-plan account will be closed about 6 months after sign-up. Anything in the plan that must outlive that (the CV demo, CI deploys) needs either an upgrade before the deadline or an accepted teardown.

findings.question: Q1b. Which services are restricted or unavailable on the Free plan, and can Relay's services be used (Lambda container images, ECR, SQS, DynamoDB, SSM Parameter Store, CloudWatch alarms/dashboards, EventBridge Scheduler, IAM OIDC providers, CloudFormation/SAM, SNS email, KMS, Budgets)?
findings.answer:
WHAT AWS SAYS FOR THE STANDARD FREE PLAN
The Free plan leaves out 'services that would rapidly consume the entire credit amount, or hardware purchases'. The examples given are Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, AWS Support subscriptions and some Marketplace offers. Lightsail is also reported as unavailable (re:Post). I found no official per-service list for the standard Free plan; the FAQ just points to aws.amazon.com/free.

THE ONLY OFFICIAL SERVICE LIST I FOUND
This list is for 'Sign up for AWS (new)', a new projects-based sign-up that is still rolling out to a limited number of customers. Every Relay service is in its Free Tier list:
- AWS Lambda (Lambda@Edge not supported)
- Amazon ECR and ECR Public (no cross-Region replication)
- Amazon SQS
- Amazon DynamoDB (no Global Tables)
- AWS Systems Manager, which covers Parameter Store
- Amazon CloudWatch and CloudWatch Logs (no cross-account observability or cross-Region dashboards)
- Amazon EventBridge
- IAM and STS
- AWS CloudFormation (no StackSets)
- AWS Serverless Application Repository
- Amazon SNS
- AWS KMS (no multi-Region keys)
- AWS Budgets, Billing and Cost Management, and Service Quotas

That same list marks AWS IAM Identity Center and AWS Organizations as NOT supported.

CONCLUSION
- Lambda container images, ECR, SQS, DynamoDB, Parameter Store, CloudWatch alarms and dashboards, EventBridge Scheduler, IAM OIDC identity providers (plain IAM), CloudFormation/SAM, SNS email, KMS and Budgets are all usable on the Free plan.
- Avoid anything that needs AWS Organizations, because it forces an upgrade to the Paid plan.

One gap: I could not find a Free-plan-specific statement about EventBridge Scheduler as a separate sub-service. It is covered under 'Amazon EventBridge'.

findings.question: Q1c. Always-free monthly limits: Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB (on-demand vs provisioned), CloudWatch, ECR, KMS (plus SNS, EventBridge Scheduler, SSM, CloudFormation)
findings.answer:
LAMBDA: 1M requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month. Applies to both x86 and Arm. Does NOT apply to functions with Provisioned Concurrency. The pricing page does not say anything specific about container images; they are billed as ordinary Lambda functions.

SQS: 'All customers can make 1 million Amazon SQS requests for free each month', counted across all Regions. The page does not say whether FIFO requests share that allowance.

DYNAMODB: 25 GB storage, 25 WCU and 25 RCU, and 2.5M Streams read requests, per Region per payer account. The free tier 'uses provisioned capacity and the DynamoDB Standard table class'. On-demand read/write request units are NOT free; they are billed from the first request. The 25 GB storage allowance does apply to on-demand tables.

CLOUDWATCH:
- 10 custom or detailed-monitoring metrics
- 10 standard-resolution alarm metrics (only alarms that list metrics directly, not Metrics Insights queries)
- 3 custom dashboards with up to 50 metrics each; automatic dashboards are free
- 1M API requests, excluding GetMetricData, GetInsightRuleReport and GetMetricWidgetImage, which are always charged
- 5 GB of logs (ingestion, archive storage and Logs Insights data scanned)
- 1,800 Live Tail minutes

ECR:
- Private repositories: 500 MB per month 'for one year' for new customers. That is a legacy 12-month offer, so post-July-2025 accounts do not get it; private storage (about $0.10 per GB-month) is paid from credits.
- Public repositories: 50 GB per month, always free.

KMS: 20,000 requests per month across Regions. AWS-managed keys such as aws/ssm have no monthly key fee. Customer-managed keys cost $1 per month.

SNS: 1M publishes, 100,000 HTTP/S deliveries and 1,000 email deliveries per month. Deliveries to SQS and Lambda are free. These figures come from secondary sources; the SNS pricing page did not render them.

EVENTBRIDGE SCHEDULER: 14,000,000 invocations per month free, then $1.00 per million.

SSM PARAMETER STORE: standard parameters and standard-throughput API calls cost nothing. Advanced parameters cost $0.05 each per month plus $0.05 per 10,000 API interactions.

CLOUDFORMATION: no charge for AWS::* resource types.

BUDGETS: see Q2.

findings.question: Q2. Exact console steps for a monthly $1 cost budget with email alert; do budgets cost anything; how delayed is billing data?
findings.answer:
ONE-TIME PREREQUISITE (only if you'll manage budgets as an IAM user)
As root, open https://console.aws.amazon.com/billing/home?#/account. Under 'IAM user and role access to Billing information', choose Edit, tick 'Activate IAM access', and choose Update. Without this, IAM users cannot open the Budgets pages even with AdministratorAccess.

OPTION A: TEMPLATE (FASTEST)
1. Open https://console.aws.amazon.com/costmanagement/ and choose Budgets in the left pane.
2. Choose 'Create budget'.
3. Under Budget setup, choose 'Use a template (simplified)'.
4. Under Templates, choose 'Monthly cost budget' ('notifies you if you exceed, or are forecasted to exceed, the budget amount'). The other templates are 'Zero spend budget', 'Daily Savings Plans coverage budget' and 'Daily reservation utilization budget'.
5. Enter a Budget name, set the budgeted amount to 1.00, and enter your email under Email recipients (up to 10 addresses).
6. Choose 'Create budget'.

Secondary sources say the template alerts at 85% actual, 100% actual and 100% forecasted.

OPTION B: CUSTOMIZE (ADVANCED), WHICH LETS YOU CONTROL CREDITS
1. Choose Create budget > 'Customize (advanced)' > Budget types: 'Cost budget' > Next.
2. Enter a Budget name.
3. Set Period = Monthly, Budget renewal type = Recurring budget, Budgeting method = Fixed, amount = 1.00.
4. Under Budget scope > Advanced options, choose 'Use unblended costs'. Do not choose 'net unblended', which is 'after all discounts and credits are applied'.
5. Next > Add an alert threshold: Threshold 100, '% of budgeted amount', Trigger 'Actual', your email. Optionally add a second alert at 100% 'Forecasted'.
6. Next > skip Attach actions > Next > Create budget.

THE CREDITS GOTCHA (important on credit accounts)
The Budgets API field CostTypes.IncludeCredit defaults to true, so a budget nets credits out of spend. On an account where credits cover everything, it can show $0 and never alert. AWS's own guidance is 'make sure the credits options is not checked, otherwise you won't track the costs if paying with credits'. After using the template, edit the budget and exclude Credits in Advanced options, or use unblended cost.

COST
- 'You can monitor and receive notifications on your budgets free of charge.'
- The first two action-enabled budgets are free; each further one costs $0.10 per day.
- Emailed budget reports cost $0.01 each.

DATA DELAY
- Budgets data is 'updated up to three times a day', with updates 'typically 8–12 hours after the previous update'.
- Billing data behind it updates 'at least once per day'.
- Actual alerts fire once per budget period.
- Forecast alerts need about 5 weeks of usage history, so a brand-new account will not get forecast alerts at first.
- Creating a budget turns on Cost Explorer, and its graph can take up to 24 hours to appear.

findings.question: Q3a. 'aws login' in AWS CLI v2: minimum version, what it does, root/IAM user support, session length, region/profile handling, credential cache
findings.answer:
VERSIONS AND WHAT IT IS
- Announced 2025-11-19. Needs AWS CLI v2 2.32.0 or newer. The CLI CHANGELOG currently shows 2.36.50 at the top.
- It is a browser-based OAuth 2.0 + PKCE sign-in using your console credentials. The CLI then manages short-term credentials for you.

WHO CAN USE IT
- Root user: no extra permissions needed.
- IAM user or role: needs the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess managed policy (signin:AuthorizeOAuth2Access and signin:CreateOAuth2Token). An identity with AdministratorAccess (Action '*') already has these.
- IAM federation also works.
- If you use IAM Identity Center, use 'aws configure sso' instead.

SESSION LENGTH
Credentials last 15 minutes and are refreshed automatically. The whole session lasts up to the principal's session duration, 12 hours at most. After that you run 'aws login' again. 'aws logout' (or 'aws logout --all') deletes the cached credentials.

PROFILE AND REGION
- 'aws login --profile NAME'.
- For a new profile, or one with no region, the CLI prompts 'AWS Region [us-east-1]:'. You can change it later with 'aws configure set region X'.
- The config file gets:
  [profile NAME]
  login_session = arn:aws:iam::<acct>:user/<name>
  region = ...
- Use 'aws login --remote' on a machine without a browser; you paste an authorization code back in.

CACHE
The token and refresh token are stored in %USERPROFILE%\.aws\login\cache on Windows. Override with AWS_LOGIN_CACHE_DIRECTORY. No long-term keys are written, but a refresh token (up to 12 hours) is on disk.

COMPATIBILITY FALLBACK
For tools that don't support login_session, add a profile with:
  credential_process = aws configure export-credentials --profile NAME --format process

findings.question: Q3b. aws login vs 'aws configure sso' vs access keys; what should a student on a personal Free-plan account use, and should they create a non-root admin first (minimal steps)?
findings.answer:
COMPARISON
- 'aws configure sso' (IAM Identity Center) needs an ORGANIZATION instance to reach AWS accounts. An account instance 'do[es] not support permission sets and therefore do[es] not support access to AWS accounts'. An organization instance needs AWS Organizations, and joining Organizations automatically upgrades a Free-plan account to Paid. The new sign-up experience also lists Identity Center and Organizations as unsupported. So SSO is the wrong tool on a Free-plan personal account.
- Access keys are long-lived secrets stored in plain text in %USERPROFILE%\.aws\credentials. Avoid them.

RECOMMENDATION
Use 'aws login' with a non-root IAM admin user that has no access keys. It works with root too, but AWS strongly advises against using root for everyday work. GitHub Actions uses its own OIDC role and needs no keys.

MINIMAL STEPS
1. As root: enable MFA on root (top-right account menu > Security credentals > Assign MFA device).
2. As root, turn on IAM billing access: Billing console > Account > 'IAM user and role access to Billing information' > Edit > tick 'Activate IAM access' > Update.
3. IAM console > Users > Create user:
   - User name, e.g. relay-admin.
   - Tick 'Provide user access to the AWS Management Console', choose 'I want to create an IAM user', set a custom password.
   - Next > 'Attach policies directly' > AdministratorAccess. This covers the signin:* actions; with a narrower policy, add SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess.
   - Create user.
   - Do NOT create access keys.
4. Sign out, then sign in at https://<account-id>.signin.aws.amazon.com/console as relay-admin and assign MFA to that user.
5. Locally: 'aws --version' (must be 2.32.0 or newer), then 'aws login --profile relay' and pick the region. Then set $env:AWS_PROFILE='relay' and run 'aws sts get-caller-identity'.

findings.question: Q3c. Do the other tools in Relay's toolchain (SAM CLI, Go SDK v2, boto3) pick up 'aws login' credentials?
findings.answer:
PYTHON (boto3)
Supported, but it requires the AWS Common Runtime (CRT) and boto3 1.41.0 or newer. Install boto3[crt].

SAM CLI
The develop branch's pyproject.toml pins boto3[crt]==1.43.83, so SAM CLI should resolve login_session profiles. This is inferred from the dependency; I found no release note that says so.

GO SDK v2
The SDK reference table says 'SDK for Go V2: No', but that looks wrong or stale. The aws-sdk-go-v2 config CHANGELOG v1.32.0 (2025-11-19) says 'Add support for AWS Login credentials (package credentials/logincreds) to the default credential chain'. The logincreds package is present in credentials v1.20.5. Use config >= v1.32.0 for relayctl.

IF ANY TOOL FAILS
Use the credential_process profile with 'aws configure export-credentials --format process'.

findings.question: Q4. SSM Parameter Store: what happens at 100 versions on PutParameter --overwrite? Can CloudFormation/SAM create SecureString parameters?
findings.answer:
100-VERSION LIMIT
- The oldest version is deleted automatically: 'After you have created 100 versions of a parameter, each time you create a new version, the oldest version of the parameter is removed from history.'
- ParameterMaxVersionLimitExceeded (HTTP 400) happens ONLY when the oldest version has a label attached. The error text is 'Version N, the oldest version, can't be deleted because it has a label associated with it. Move the label...'.
- So a watermark written every 2 minutes is fine as long as you never label its versions.
- Other errors to handle: TooManyUpdates for concurrent writes, and ThrottlingException under the default standard-throughput quota.
- Standard tier: 4 KB values, 10,000 parameters per Region, no charge.

SECURESTRING IN CLOUDFORMATION / SAM
Not supported. AWS::SSM::Parameter Type allows only 'String | StringList': 'Parameters of type SecureString are not supported by AWS CloudFormation.' PutParameter docs repeat this.

What to do instead:
- Create the Salesforce client ID and secret by hand, e.g. 'aws ssm put-parameter --name /relay/sf/client_secret --type SecureString --value ...'. With no --key-id it uses the AWS-managed aws/ssm key: no monthly key fee, and KMS requests count against the 20k free per month.
- Read them at runtime with WithDecryption=true.
- Keep only non-secret String parameters, such as the watermark and chaos flags, in the SAM template.
- The '{{resolve:ssm-secure:...}}' dynamic reference does NOT work in Lambda environment variables.

findings.question: Q5. Lambda on a new account with a concurrent-executions quota of 10: does ReservedConcurrentExecutions fail? What is the default quota in 2026?
findings.answer:
THE QUOTA
- The documented default is 1,000 concurrent executions per Region.
- The Lambda quotas page now warns: 'New AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas... AWS raises these quotas automatically based on your usage.'
- 10 is the commonly observed value on new accounts; a GitHub issue opened 2026-09-06 shows 10 against the 1,000 default.

WHY RESERVED CONCURRENCY FAILS
- The docs say you can reserve up to 'Unreserved account concurrency value minus 100'.
- Real deployments on low-quota accounts fail with 'Specified ReservedConcurrentExecutions for function decreases account's UnreservedConcurrentExecution below its minimum value of [10]'.
- So at a quota of 10, any ReservedConcurrentExecutions of 1 or more fails and the CloudFormation/SAM stack rolls back. Do not put it in template.yaml.

ALTERNATIVES
- Cap the worker with the SQS event source mapping's ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency (2 to 1,000). It reserves nothing and costs nothing. Note it turns off Lambda's idle optimization down to 2 pollers.
- Pause the poller by setting the EventBridge Scheduler schedule State to DISABLED.
- Ask for an increase via Service Quotas > AWS Lambda > Concurrent executions. Approval is not guaranteed on new accounts.

RELATED SQS SETTINGS
With only 10 concurrency, throttling is likely. Follow the Lambda guidance: queue visibility timeout at least 6 times the function timeout, and redrive maxReceiveCount of at least 5, so throttled batches don't land in the DLQ early.

findings.question: Q8. Lambda base images: is public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.12 current and when is python3.12 deprecated? Is provided:al2023 right for Go? Is the Runtime Interface Emulator still bundled?
findings.answer:
PYTHON 3.12
- public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.12 is current and runs on Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023) minimal.
- python3.12 deprecation: Oct 31, 2028. Function creates blocked from Nov 30, 2028; updates blocked from Jan 10, 2029.
- Newer options: python3.13 and python3.14, both deprecating Jun 30, 2029. python3.15 is in public preview with GA targeted for Nov 2026.
- Avoid 3.10 and 3.11: they run on Amazon Linux 2 (AL2), and 3.10 deprecates Oct 31, 2026.
- AWS does not send deprecation notifications for container-image functions; you must rebuild from the latest base image yourself.

GO
- public.ecr.aws/lambda/provided:al2023 is the correct and recommended base ('OS-only Runtime', deprecation Jun 30, 2029).
- provided.al2 was deprecated Jul 31, 2026. go1.x was deprecated in Jan 2024.
- AWS's Dockerfile: 'FROM golang:<ver> AS build', then 'go build -tags lambda.norpc -o main', then 'FROM public.ecr.aws/lambda/provided:al2023', 'COPY --from=build .../main ./main', 'ENTRYPOINT ["./main"]'.
- The binary does not have to be named 'bootstrap' for images; that name is required for .zip on provided.al2023.
- Include github.com/aws/aws-lambda-go/lambda.
- My own recommendation, not stated in the AWS doc: build with CGO_ENABLED=0. The Debian trixie golang image has a newer glibc than AL2023, so a cgo-linked binary can fail at runtime.

RUNTIME INTERFACE EMULATOR (RIE)
- Still bundled. The AWS base images 'are preloaded with a language runtime, a runtime interface client... and a runtime interface emulator'.
- For provided.al2023: 'The runtime interface emulator is included' at /usr/local/bin/aws-lambda-rie.
- Test with: docker run -p 9000:8080 --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/aws-lambda-rie img ./main, then POST to http://localhost:9000/2015-03-31/functions/function/invocations.
- SAM CLI 1.166.0 bundles RIE 1.37.

findings.question: Plan-specific cost and quota risks found while researching (PLAN.md lines 23, 85-88, 97, 105, 177-181)
findings.answer:
1. 'Nothing runs (or costs) when idle' is not quite true.
   - An SQS event source mapping keeps long-polling even with an empty queue: about 5 pollers, which can drop to 2 when idle. That optimization is 'not available when you enable the maximum concurrency setting'.
   - Each poller's long polls are SQS requests. My estimate, not an AWS figure: roughly 260k to 650k requests per month per mapping. That is inside the 1M free, but it is not zero, and two mappings could approach it.
2. DynamoDB 'on-demand' is not free.
   - Only provisioned 25 RCU/WCU are free, per Region.
   - For three tables at 5/5 each, count every GSI's provisioned capacity toward the 25.
   - Don't enable auto scaling. It creates CloudWatch alarms that would eat into the 10 free alarm metrics. This is my inference, not verified in this session.
3. CloudWatch custom metrics are counted per unique name and dimension combination. Six metric names with several dimension values can exceed the 10 free.
4. ECR private storage is billed against credits, since the 12-month 500 MB offer does not apply to new accounts. Add an ECR lifecycle policy keeping the last N images.
5. SSM SecureString: see Q4. It must be created outside SAM.
6. ReservedConcurrentExecutions: see Q5. It will fail on a 10-concurrency account.
7. The Free plan closes the account at 6 months or when credits run out: see Q1a.
8. The repo lives under OneDrive (C:\Users\luckf\OneDrive\Desktop\EverPure Relay).
   - SAM warns about Windows MAX_PATH.
   - Docker bind mounts from OneDrive-synced folders can cause file-lock and sync problems. This is general experience, not an AWS doc.
   - Consider enabling long paths and moving the repo to a non-synced path.
