findings.question: 1. Lambda SQS event source mapping with ReportBatchItemFailures: if the function calls ChangeMessageVisibility on a message and then returns it in batchItemFailures, does the new visibility hold? Does Lambda change or reset the visibility of failed messages? Caveats?
findings.answer:
Yes, this works as a per-message exponential backoff, with caveats. The AWS docs never state the pattern directly. It follows from behaviour they do document:

(a) With ReportBatchItemFailures on, Lambda deletes only the messages you did not list in `batchItemFailures`. It leaves the listed ones in flight and does nothing else to them. No AWS page I read says that Lambda calls ChangeMessageVisibility or resets visibility on failed items. The Lambda error-handling page says a failed message reappears once its visibility timeout runs out.

(b) ChangeMessageVisibility applies immediately and counts from the moment of the call. The range is 0 to 43,200 s. It needs the receipt handle from the current receive, which is the `receiptHandle` field on each record. The new value is not kept for later receives: the next receive falls back to the queue default.

So the pattern works: call ChangeMessageVisibility(QueueUrl, receiptHandle, base*2^n + jitter), then put the `messageId` in `batchItemFailures`. Community write-ups and 2026 blog posts describe the same behaviour.

Caveats:
- If the handler throws, or times out, the whole batch counts as failed. The same happens if the response has invalid JSON, an empty or null `itemIdentifier`, a wrong key name, or a messageId that is not in the batch. An empty or null `batchItemFailures` list means full success, so every message is deleted. Visibility changes you already made still hold in the failure case. The other messages come back after the queue's visibility timeout.
- If you back off a message but forget to list it, Lambda deletes it and it is lost without a trace.
- The Powertools BatchProcessor raises BatchProcessingError by default when every record fails, and that becomes a whole-batch failure. Set `raise_on_entire_batch_failure=False`.
- Receipt handles are only valid for the current receive. With an old handle, ChangeMessageVisibility can fail (MessageNotInflight or ReceiptHandleIsInvalid). DeleteMessage with an old handle returns success but may not delete.
- Visibility is capped at 12 hours from receipt. Asking for more time than remains returns an error; SQS does not clamp the value.
- With ReportBatchItemFailures, Lambda does not reduce polling because of reported failures. Thrown errors do make Lambda reduce concurrency.
- IAM: the AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole managed policy only has ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage and GetQueueAttributes. You need `sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility`, which SAM's SQSPollerPolicy template includes.

findings.question: 2. When is a message moved to the DLQ relative to ApproximateReceiveCount and maxReceiveCount? Do throttled invocations increment the receive count? AWS recommendations for maxReceiveCount and visibility timeout vs function timeout. Max visibility timeout.
findings.answer:
How the move works:
- `RedrivePolicy` = {deadLetterTargetArn, maxReceiveCount}. SQS moves a message to the DLQ when its receive count exceeds maxReceiveCount. The default is 10 if you leave it out.
- With maxReceiveCount=5, the worker sees the message 5 times, with ApproximateReceiveCount 1 through 5. The move happens on the next receive attempt, after the 5th attempt's visibility timeout expires. So a long backoff on the 5th failure delays arrival in the DLQ.
- ApproximateReceiveCount counts receives across all queues where the message was not deleted.
- New behaviour in the 2025/26 docs: on a standard queue with maxReceiveCount > 3, a message received 3 or more times without being deleted is moved to the back of the queue. ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage then leaves these poison-pill messages out.

Throttling:
- When an invocation is throttled, Lambda keeps retrying the batch it already received. It stops once the message's visibility timeout expires, and the message goes back to the queue.
- The next poll is a new receive, so the count goes up by one. Sustained throttling can therefore push messages into the DLQ. The AWS Compute Blog on maximum concurrency showed 9 messages dead-lettered under reserved-concurrency throttling, and none when ESM MaximumConcurrency was used instead.

AWS recommendations:
- maxReceiveCount of at least 5.
- Queue visibility timeout of at least 6x the function timeout, plus MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds if you use one.
- Lambda rejects the event source mapping if the function timeout is longer than the queue's visibility timeout. It checks this on create and update.
- If you use reserved concurrency, set it to at least 5, and at least as high as the ESM MaximumConcurrency. MaximumConcurrency accepts 2 to 1,000.

Limits:
- Visibility timeout: 0 to 43,200 s (12 h), default 30 s.
- MessageRetentionPeriod: 60 s to 1,209,600 s (14 days), default 4 days.
- On standard queues, expiry is based on the original enqueue time, even after the move to the DLQ. So give the DLQ a longer retention than the source queue.
- The DLQ must be the same queue type, in the same account and region.

Redrive:
- StartMessageMoveTask only works on DLQs whose sources are SQS queues.
- Leave DestinationArn out to send messages back to their original source queue.
- Maximum 500 messages/s, and one active task per queue.

findings.question: 3. DynamoDB TransactWriteItems: behaviour when one item's ConditionExpression fails, CancellationReasons shape in boto3, codes, ALL_OLD per item, retryable errors, ClientRequestToken semantics.
findings.answer:
Basics:
- Up to 100 actions (Put, Update, Delete, ConditionCheck), 4 MB in total, same account and region, and no two actions on the same item. Either everything succeeds or nothing does.
- Any failed condition cancels the whole request with TransactionCanceledException (HTTP 400). The AWS SDKs do not retry this exception automatically.

boto3 shape:
- Catch `client.exceptions.TransactionCanceledException as e`.
- `e.response['CancellationReasons']` is a top-level list, next to `e.response['Error']`. It has one entry per TransactItems element, in request order.
- Each entry looks like {'Code': str, 'Message': str, 'Item': {attr: AttributeValue}}.
- An item with no error has Code set to the literal string 'None' and no Message.

Codes: None, ConditionalCheckFailed, ItemCollectionSizeLimitExceeded, TransactionConflict, ProvisionedThroughputExceeded, ThrottlingError, ValidationError.

ALL_OLD:
- `ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure: 'ALL_OLD' | 'NONE'` can be set on each Put, Update, Delete and ConditionCheck.
- With ALL_OLD, the existing item comes back as `Item` in that item's CancellationReason, in low-level AttributeValue form such as {'version': {'N': '...'}}.
- An old boto3 issue (#2657, closed as stale) reported the values missing from ClientError even though the raw response contained them. Add a test against real DynamoDB.
- Single-item PutItem also supports ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure and returns `Item` on ConditionalCheckFailedException.

Retry classification:
- Do not retry: ConditionalCheckFailed (it is the business signal for duplicate or stale), ValidationError, IdempotentParameterMismatchException, ResourceNotFoundException, ValidationException.
- Retry with backoff: TransactionConflict (another write in progress on the same item, e.g. the same customer), ThrottlingError and ProvisionedThroughputExceeded inside the reasons, and the top-level ThrottlingException, ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, RequestLimitExceeded, InternalServerError and ServiceUnavailable. The SDK already retries the top-level ones.
- The docs say TransactWriteItems is safe to retry after a 500.
- Retry TransactionInProgressException with the same token; the SDK does this.
- ItemCollectionSizeLimitExceeded only applies to tables with LSIs.

Cost: each item takes 2 underlying writes (prepare and commit). Cancelled transactions still use capacity.

ClientRequestToken:
- 1 to 36 characters. It makes the call idempotent for 10 minutes after the first request with that token completes.
- A repeat call with the token after a success returns success without changing anything, and reports read capacity.
- After 10 minutes, the same token counts as a new request.
- Same token with different parameters inside the window gives IdempotentParameterMismatch.
- boto3 fills the token in automatically if you omit it. That only covers SDK-level retries of a single call, not SQS redeliveries minutes later.

findings.question: 4. SQS standard queues: at-least-once delivery and no ordering guarantee (quote the docs). Max batch size for the Lambda trigger.
findings.answer:
The SQS developer guide says: "Standard queues ensure at-least-once message delivery". The same page goes on to say that more than one copy of a message may be delivered and that messages can occasionally arrive out of order. Ordering is only best effort.

The at-least-once page explains the cause. If a storage server is unavailable during a delete, that copy is not deleted and can be received again. Applications must be idempotent. The Lambda docs say the same about event source mappings: every event is processed at least once, duplicates can happen, and AWS strongly recommends idempotent function code.

Lambda trigger limits:
- BatchSize defaults to 10. The maximum is 10,000 for standard queues and 10 for FIFO queues. SAM's SQS event allows 1 to 10,000.
- A batch size over 10 requires MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds of at least 1.
- The batching window goes up to 5 minutes and is only for standard queues.
- A batch is also capped by the 6 MB synchronous invocation payload, and SQS/Lambda metadata counts toward it.
- A single ReceiveMessage call returns at most 10 messages. The ESM combines several calls into one batch.
- The current maximum SQS message size is 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes).

findings.question: 5. EventBridge Scheduler: delivery semantics, flexible time windows, and enable/disable flag in SAM.
findings.answer:
Delivery:
- EventBridge Scheduler delivers to targets at least once. A delivery counts as successful when the target responds.
- Retries are set with RetryPolicy: MaximumRetryAttempts 0 to 185, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds 60 to 86,400. Retries use exponential backoff.
- You can add an SQS DeadLetterConfig for deliveries that fail.
- Scheduler invokes a Lambda target asynchronously, so Lambda's async rules also apply. On a function error Lambda retries twice by default, waiting 1 minute and then 2 minutes. On throttles or 5xx it retries for up to 6 hours. Duplicate events can arrive even when nothing fails.
- In practice the poller can run twice for the same tick. A failed run can also re-run 1 or 2 minutes later, overlapping the next 2-minute tick.

Flexible time windows:
- FlexibleTimeWindow is required on AWS::Scheduler::Schedule.
- Mode is OFF (exact time) or FLEXIBLE. FLEXIBLE needs MaximumWindowInMinutes, and the invocation happens somewhere inside that window after the scheduled time. Example: a 15-minute window on an hourly schedule.
- I believe the range is 1 to 1440 minutes. I did not confirm this on the pages I read.

Expressions: `rate(value unit)` with minute(s), hour(s) or day(s); a 6-field `cron(...)`; or `at(...)` for one-time schedules. ScheduleExpressionTimezone is optional.

Enable/disable in SAM:
- The `ScheduleV2` event on AWS::Serverless::Function has `State`, accepting ENABLED or DISABLED. SAM passes it straight to AWS::Scheduler::Schedule `State`, and changing it updates without interruption.
- Example: a template Parameter `PollerScheduleState` with AllowedValues [ENABLED, DISABLED], used as `State: !Ref PollerScheduleState`.
- ScheduleV2 also supports FlexibleTimeWindow, RetryPolicy, DeadLetterConfig (with `Type: SQS`, SAM creates the queue), Input, GroupName, StartDate/EndDate and OmitName.
- By default SAM names the schedule `<FunctionLogicalId><EventName>`, without the stack name.
- To pause the worker instead, use `Enabled: false` on the SQS event.

findings.question: 6. SAM PackageType Image, sam deploy --resolve-image-repos, and 7-day log retention for every Lambda (explicit LogGroup vs LoggingConfig.LogGroup); ordering pitfalls.
findings.answer:
Image functions:
- Set `PackageType: Image`. `ImageConfig` (Command/EntryPoint) is optional.
- Add a resource-level `Metadata` block: `Dockerfile` (file name), `DockerContext` (directory), and optionally `DockerTag`, `DockerBuildArgs` and `DockerImage`.
- `sam build` builds the image, using the legacy Docker builder unless you pass `--use-buildkit`.
- A Metadata-based build takes precedence over `ImageUri`. If both are present, ImageUri is ignored.
- If the base image is multi-arch, SAM builds for the host's architecture. Pin an architecture-specific base image and set `Architectures` to match.

Deploy:
- `sam deploy --resolve-image-repos` creates ECR repositories automatically for non-guided deploys. It is ignored when you use `--guided`.
- If you later remove a function from the template, SAM deletes its auto-created repo.
- The alternatives are `--image-repository`, or `--image-repositories Fn=<uri>` for each function.
- The SAM CLI design issue #2856, which I saw only in search results, says these repos live in a separate companion stack. I found no documented way to set lifecycle policies on them.

Logs:
- By default, CloudWatch creates `/aws/lambda/<function name>` on the first invoke, and it never expires. SAM has no retention property; the 2019 feature request (issue #972) is closed.
- Pattern A: an `AWS::Logs::LogGroup` with `LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${Fn}` and `RetentionInDays: 7`. Because the name references the function, CloudFormation creates the function first. If the function runs before the log group resource exists, Lambda creates the group itself, and the stack then fails with 'already exists'. The SQS event source mapping or the schedule can trigger that run straight away. The same failure happens if an earlier stack deletion left the group behind. This pitfall is my reasoning from the documented behaviour; I did not find an AWS page that states it.
- Pattern B (recommended): create the log group first (`RetentionInDays: 7`) and point the function at it with `LoggingConfig: {LogGroup: !Ref WorkerLogGroup, LogFormat: Text|JSON}`. The function then depends on the log group, so the group is created before the function and deleted after it, and Lambda never creates one on its own.
- LoggingConfig properties: LogGroup, LogFormat (Text or JSON), ApplicationLogLevel (TRACE to FATAL), SystemLogLevel (DEBUG, INFO, WARN).
- Custom log group names must not start with `aws/`.
- The execution role needs logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents. AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole covers both.
- Another option is to give the function an explicit FunctionName and add DependsOn from the function to the log group.

findings.question: 7. CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format: minimal JSON, does each unique dimension combination count as a separate billed metric, free-tier custom metric count.
findings.answer:
Minimal EMF document, printed as a single JSON line to stdout:
{"_aws":{"Timestamp":<epoch ms>,"CloudWatchMetrics":[{"Namespace":"Relay","Dimensions":[["Service"]],"Metrics":[{"Name":"OrdersWritten","Unit":"Count"}]}]},"Service":"worker","OrdersWritten":1,"eventKey":"..."}

Rules:
- `_aws.CloudWatchMetrics` and `_aws.Timestamp` (milliseconds) are required.
- Each directive needs Namespace, Dimensions (an array of DimensionSets) and Metrics.
- Each metric has Name, plus optional Unit and StorageResolution (1 or 60, default 60).
- Every referenced dimension and metric must be a top-level member of the JSON object, not nested.
- Dimension values must be strings of up to 1,024 characters. Metric values must be numbers, or arrays of up to 100 numbers.
- Up to 100 metrics per directive and 30 keys per DimensionSet. The whole event can be up to 1 MB.
- Extra top-level fields such as eventKey are just log data you can query in Logs Insights. They do not create metrics.
- EMF extraction is at-least-once, so duplicate metric values can occasionally occur.

Billing:
- Each DimensionSet creates a separate metric. CloudWatch bills every unique combination of metric name and dimension values as its own custom metric.
- The EMF spec specifically warns that high-cardinality dimensions such as requestId blow up metric counts.
- Charges are prorated by the hour and only apply in hours when the metric is sent.
- Price: $0.30 per metric per month for the first 10,000.
- EMF lines are also billed as log ingestion, $0.50/GB in us-east-1 after the free tier.

Free tier (always free, not limited to 12 months):
- 10 custom metrics (custom metrics and detailed-monitoring metrics combined)
- 1M API requests
- 10 alarm metrics
- 3 dashboards of up to 50 metrics each
- 5 GB of log data (ingestion, archive and Logs Insights scanning)

findings.question: 8. GitHub Actions OIDC to AWS: thumbprint still required? Trust policy conditions, configure-aws-credentials current major version, and can the provider/role be created by the same stack the workflow deploys?
findings.answer:
Thumbprint: not required.
- IAM checks the IdP's JWKS TLS certificate against its own library of trusted root CAs. It only falls back to thumbprints when the certificate is not from a trusted CA, cannot be retrieved, or TLS 1.3 is required.
- `ThrumbprintList` on AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider is optional. If you leave it out, IAM fetches the top intermediate CA thumbprint itself.
- The configure-aws-credentials README says a thumbprint is no longer necessary and is ignored if you provide one.

Provider and trust policy:
- Provider URL: `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. Client ID/audience: `sts.amazonaws.com`, which is also the action's default.
- Trust policy: Principal Federated = `arn:aws:iam::<acct>:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com`, Action `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.
- Conditions: StringEquals `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud` = `sts.amazonaws.com`, and StringEquals `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` = the exact sub value.

New in 2026:
- GitHub announced immutable subject claims in a changelog post on 2026-04-23.
- Repos created on or after 15 July 2026, repos renamed or transferred after that date, and repos that opted in now send `repo:OWNER@OWNER_ID/REPO@REPO_ID:ref:refs/heads/main`. Older repos that have not opted in still send `repo:OWNER/REPO:ref:refs/heads/main`.
- If the trust policy uses the legacy form and the repo sends the immutable one, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity fails.
- The IDs appear in the token as `repository_owner_id` and `repository_id`. I believe the GitHub REST API also returns them as `owner.id` and `id`, but I did not check that in the docs.
- A job that uses `environment:` gets an environment-based sub instead of a branch-based one.

Workflow:
- Set `permissions: id-token: write` and `contents: read`.
- Use `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`. v6.0.0 came out 2026-02-04; its breaking change is the move to node24, which needs runner v2.327.1 or later. The latest is v6.3.0, released 2026-09-15. You can pin `@v6.3.0` or a commit SHA.

Same stack or separate: bootstrap it separately.
- The workflow has to assume the role before it can run its first deploy, so the role must already exist.
- IAM allows only one OIDC provider per URL in an account. Creating it inside the app stack fails if one already exists, and it ties the provider to that stack's lifecycle.
- A failed update, rollback or `sam delete` of the app stack could change or remove the role CI depends on.
- Letting CI edit its own role is privilege escalation.
- Recommended: a one-time bootstrap stack deployed from your laptop with admin credentials and CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM, containing the provider and the deploy role.

findings.question: Extra: Lambda concurrency constraints on a new AWS account (affects reserved concurrency and poller overlap control)
findings.answer:
The Lambda quotas page now opens with a warning: new AWS accounts get reduced concurrency and memory quotas, which AWS raises automatically as the account is used. It does not give the starting number; community reports usually say 10.

You can only reserve concurrency up to the unreserved account concurrency minus 100. On a low-quota account, any `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` in the template will fail to deploy. ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 1 on the poller, as a way to stop overlapping runs, falls into this trap.

What to use instead:
- For the worker, set the SQS event's `ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency` (2 to 1,000). It does not reserve concurrency.
- For the poller, rely on idempotent downstream processing, or use a DynamoDB conditional lease or watermark.

Other current limits: async invocation payload 1 MB, synchronous payload 6 MB, function timeout up to 900 s, container images up to 10 GB uncompressed.

findings.question: Extra: SQS CloudWatch metric semantics that affect Relay's alarms
findings.answer:
- ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage on a standard queue leaves out messages received 3 or more times without being deleted. SQS moves those to the back of the queue, and this happens even when a redrive policy is set.
- So during an ERP outage, when every message fails repeatedly, the 'worker is stuck' age alarm may never fire. Messages still in backoff are also in flight, not visible.
- For the DLQ, use ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, as AWS recommends.
- NumberOfMessagesSent on the DLQ counts messages you send there manually, such as Relay's permanent errors. It does not count automatic moves under maxReceiveCount.
- ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible can briefly report non-zero values that are not real. Alarm on several datapoints in a row.
- SQS metrics are only emitted while the queue is active.

recommendations: Worker handler contract: never raise out of the handler. Wrap each record and return {"batchItemFailures":[{"itemIdentifier": messageId}]}. For a transient failure, first call ChangeMessageVisibility(QueueUrl from an env var, record['receiptHandle'], min(base*2^(n-1) + jitter, 900)), where n = int(record['attributes']['ApproximateReceiveCount']). Then always list the message, even if the ChangeMessageVisibility call itself failed; the queue's visibility timeout is the fallback. If you use Powertools BatchProcessor, set raise_on_entire_batch_failure=False.

When n reaches maxReceiveCount (5), skip the backoff or set visibility to 0. SQS only dead-letters on the next receive, so a long backoff on attempt 5 delays the DLQ alarm. Document that 'after 5 receives' means the move happens on the 6th receive attempt.

Permanent errors: SendMessage to the DLQ with a `reason` MessageAttribute, then leave the message out of batchItemFailures so Lambda deletes the original. If the SendMessage fails, treat it as transient. The SQS event does not grant these permissions: add SQSPollerPolicy on the main queue (it includes sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility) and SQSSendMessagePolicy on the DLQ. Because these messages were sent manually rather than moved by the redrive policy, relayctl redrive should pass an explicit DestinationArn to StartMessageMoveTask, or re-send the messages itself. Returning them to the 'original source' may not work for them (my inference).

Queue settings: worker Timeout 30 s, so main-queue VisibilityTimeout ≥ 180 s (6x, plus any batching window). RedrivePolicy maxReceiveCount 5; set it explicitly because the default is 10. DLQ MessageRetentionPeriod 1,209,600 s (14 days), longer than the source queue's (e.g. the 4-day default). ESM: FunctionResponseTypes [ReportBatchItemFailures], BatchSize 10, ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency 2 to 5. Do not set ReservedConcurrentExecutions, because new-account quotas can make the deploy fail.

Idempotent ERP write: in TransactWriteItems, make the order Put conditional (attribute_not_exists(pk) OR version < :v) with ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure=ALL_OLD. Store the version as a Number (epoch ms of SystemModstamp) so comparisons are numeric. On TransactionCanceledException, read e.response['CancellationReasons'][ORDER_INDEX]. If the code is ConditionalCheckFailed, compare Item['version']['N'] with the incoming version: equal counts as DuplicatesSkipped, older incoming counts as StaleVersionsDropped, and both are successes with no retry. TransactionConflict, ThrottlingError and ProvisionedThroughputExceeded are transient. ValidationError is permanent (send to the DLQ). Make the chaos flag raise the same shape as a real ThrottlingError so the tests exercise the real classifier.

Do not use the event key as ClientRequestToken. `OpportunityId:SystemModstamp` is about 47 characters, over the 36-character limit, and the token only lasts 10 minutes. Let boto3 fill it in. Idempotency across SQS redeliveries comes from the version condition, which matches the plan's 'no outbox needed' claim. Budget 2 WCU per item per transaction, including cancelled duplicates.

Poller: EventBridge Scheduler (at-least-once) invokes Lambda asynchronously, and async invocations get 2 retries by default. Set `EventInvokeConfig: {MaximumRetryAttempts: 0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 60}` on the poller so a failed run does not overlap the next 2-minute tick. Accept that duplicate or overlapping runs will happen. That is safe only if the watermark advances after SendMessage succeeds; a watermark that moves backwards only republishes, which the worker absorbs. Optionally keep the watermark in DynamoDB with a 'only advance if greater' conditional update, since SSM PutParameter has no compare-and-set.

SAM schedules: add Parameter PollerScheduleState (AllowedValues ENABLED/DISABLED). Poller: ScheduleV2 {ScheduleExpression: rate(2 minutes), FlexibleTimeWindow: {Mode: OFF}, State: !Ref PollerScheduleState}. Reconciler: ScheduleV2 {ScheduleExpression: cron(0 2 * * ? *), ScheduleExpressionTimezone: <your IANA zone>, FlexibleTimeWindow: {Mode: FLEXIBLE, MaximumWindowInMinutes: 15}}. Set FlexibleTimeWindow explicitly because CloudFormation requires it.

Log retention: for each of the 3 functions, define `AWS::Logs::LogGroup` (RetentionInDays: 7, e.g. /relay/ingest, /relay/worker, /relay/reconciler) and set `LoggingConfig: {LogGroup: !Ref <LogGroup>}` on the function. The log group is then created first, and there is no 'already exists' race with Lambda's own auto-creation. Do not name custom groups starting with 'aws/'. Before switching LogFormat to JSON, check that EMF lines are still extracted.

Images: build with Metadata (Dockerfile/DockerContext/DockerTag) and deploy with `sam deploy --resolve-image-repos --resolve-s3 --no-confirm-changeset --no-fail-on-empty-changeset --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM`. The plan wants commit-SHA tags for rollback, which conflicts with this: DockerTag is static and ImageUri is ignored when Metadata is present. Either accept SAM's tags (rollback = redeploy the previous commit), or build and push in CI and pass ImageUri as a template parameter without Metadata. Auto-created repos have no lifecycle policy, so ECR storage grows with every commit. The plan's 'a few cents' ECR estimate assumes 3 images; add an ECR lifecycle rule (keep the last ~5), which means owning the repos in the bootstrap stack and passing --image-repositories. Match `Architectures` to the base image (x86_64 on GitHub-hosted ubuntu runners).

EMF: use namespace Relay with one fixed DimensionSet ([["Service"]]) for all six metrics. That is 6 custom metrics, within the 10-metric free tier. Never use eventKey or OpportunityId as a dimension; keep them as plain JSON fields for Logs Insights. Watch for extra metrics that silently add up, such as Powertools' ColdStart metric or a second DimensionSet. Alarms on EMF metrics need TreatMissingData: notBreaching, because nothing is emitted when there is no activity.

Alarms: DLQ alarm on AWS/SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 0 for the DLQ. The main-queue ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage alarm will not catch messages that fail 3 or more times, so the plan's 'worker stuck' alarm is weaker than it looks during an ERP outage. Add ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible or ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible over several datapoints, and the Lambda Errors alarm on ingest. Stay within the 10 free alarm metrics.

OIDC: create a separate one-time bootstrap stack from your laptop. It holds AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider (Url https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, ClientIdList [sts.amazonaws.com], no ThumbprintList); if a provider already exists in the account, reference it instead. It also holds the deploy role and, optionally, ECR repos with lifecycle rules and the SAM artifact bucket. The Relay repo is almost certainly created after 15 July 2026, so the trust policy sub must use the immutable form: `repo:OWNER@OWNER_ID/REPO@REPO_ID:ref:refs/heads/main`, with StringEquals on aud = sts.amazonaws.com. In the workflow, use `permissions: {id-token: write, contents: read}` and `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6` (or pin v6.3.0 by SHA). GitHub-hosted runners already meet the node24 requirement.

Testing: unit-test the handler contract (which IDs are listed, backoff math, DLQ send, and that a backed-off ID is never omitted) against a fake SQS client. Do not rely on LocalStack to reproduce visibility, receive-count or DLQ timing exactly (my inference, not verified). Check 'reaches the DLQ after 5 attempts' in a real-AWS smoke test with a short base backoff.

Update PLAN.md wording: the failure-table row saying 'After 5 receives, SQS moves it to the DLQ' should say the move happens on the next receive after the 5th failure. The log-retention line should name the LoggingConfig + explicit LogGroup pattern. The CI section should state that the OIDC provider and role are bootstrapped outside the app stack and use GitHub's immutable sub claim.

A third-party issue says pinning localstack/localstack:4.4.0 avoids the token. I could not confirm which pre-2026.03 tag is the last token-free one. Sources read: https://blog.localstack.cloud/localstack-for-aws-release-2026-03-0/ , https://blog.localstack.cloud/localstack-single-image-next-steps/ , https://docs.localstack.cloud/aws/getting-started/auth-token/ , https://docs.localstack.cloud/aws/licensing/ ; snippet only: https://github.com/game-ci/unity-builder/issues/822

issues.title: Nothing in the local stack triggers the worker or the poller: the Lambda emulator only exposes an invoke endpoint
issues.plan_section: Docker > Local stack ('The deployed functions, invoked through the emulator'); Testing strategy (Integration, Failure injection); 1.3/1.4 'Done when'
issues.detail: The Lambda Runtime Interface Emulator (RIE) in the AWS base images serves only POST /2015-03-31/functions/function/invocations on port 8080. It does not poll SQS, run schedules, delete messages or read batchItemFailures. Those behaviours belong to Lambda's SQS event source mapping, which exists only on AWS or inside LocalStack's own Lambda service. LocalStack's Lambda docs illustrate container-image functions with a Pro sample, require the image to be pushed to LocalStack's ECR, and need docker.sock mounted. Treat 'run the same image under LocalStack's event source mapping' as unavailable on the free Hobby plan unless proven otherwise. So as written, `docker compose up` produces a queue that fills and a worker nobody calls. The duplicate, out-of-order and 100%-failure tests cannot pass. Confidence: high on the RIE; medium-high on LocalStack image support being Pro-only. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/go-image.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html , https://docs.localstack.cloud/aws/services/lambda/ , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-errorhandling.html
issues.suggestion:
Add a small test-harness service. It is test code, not a product component: e.g. tests/harness/sqs_pump.py, run as compose service `event-source`. It should:
- Loop ReceiveMessage against LocalStack with MaxNumberOfMessages=10, WaitTimeSeconds=20, AttributeNames=['All'] and MessageAttributeNames=['All'].
- Build the exact Lambda SQS event: Records[] with messageId, receiptHandle, body, attributes (including ApproximateReceiveCount), messageAttributes, md5OfBody, eventSource 'aws:sqs', eventSourceARN and awsRegion.
- POST the event to http://worker:8080/2015-03-31/functions/function/invocations.
- Call DeleteMessageBatch for every record not listed in batchItemFailures.
- On a non-200 response or an invalid body, delete nothing, so the whole batch reappears as it would on AWS.
Leave maxReceiveCount and the DLQ move to the SQS redrive policy, which LocalStack implements. Replace EventBridge Scheduler locally with a ticker loop, or have tests POST {} to the ingest emulator. Give the Lambda containers AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localstack:4566 and dummy credentials, and never set these in template.yaml. State in PLAN.md that the pump only emulates the event source mapping. The FunctionResponseTypes setting and real visibility behaviour are proven only by a deployed check (see the CI/CD issue).

issues.title: Watermark misses records whose transactions commit late
issues.plan_section: Happy path steps 1–2 and the '>=' paragraph; Failure handling row 'Poller misses a record'
issues.detail: SystemModstamp is set when the write happens, not when the transaction commits and becomes visible. A long transaction (bulk update, trigger or flow chain) can commit after the poller has read a later-stamped row and moved the watermark past it. The late row's stamp is below the watermark, so `>=` never returns it. Salesforce's replication API returns latestDateCovered to protect against long-running processes. Commercial replicators add a 'transaction consistency timeout' overlap: Qlik documents missing Salesforce records caused by exactly this, fixed by widening the window. The plan blames misses on 'watermark bug, Salesforce outage, clock skew'. But an outage makes the poll fail without advancing, and clock skew is irrelevant when the watermark comes from Salesforce data. Commit lag is the real cause. The reconciler repairs it only nightly, and only when the order is missing entirely; a missed update is never repaired (see reconciler issue). Confidence: medium-high. The mechanism is standard, but Salesforce's getUpdated page returned 403 to me, so it is cited through secondary sources. Sources read: https://community.qlik.com/t5/Official-Support-Articles/Qlik-Replicate-Addressing-Missing-Records-in-CDC-When-Loading/ta-p/2103614 , https://andyinthecloud.com/2016/03/26/monitoring-record-activity-via-data-replication-apis/ ; not readable (403): https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api.meta/api/sforce_api_calls_getupdated.htm
issues.suggestion: Close each poll window a safety lag behind Salesforce's clock. Query `SystemModstamp >= :wm AND SystemModstamp < :upper`, where upper = Salesforce server time (from the HTTP Date header of the token or query response) minus L. L is configurable, 2–5 minutes. Follow nextRecordsUrl until done=true, publish, then set the watermark to upper, not to the newest row's stamp. Half-open windows tile time exactly: equal timestamps are never split, nothing is republished each poll, and Lambda clock skew stops mattering. Keep `>=` on the lower bound so interview question 4 still applies. Change the happy-path promise to 'within about 2 minutes + L' and reword the 'Poller misses a record' row to name commit lag. Add a Go test in which the fake Salesforce inserts a row stamped behind the current watermark.

issues.title: '>=' with watermark = newest published stamp republishes the boundary forever; LIMIT can deadlock; pagination unspecified
issues.plan_section: Happy path step 2 and the '>=' paragraph; Observability (EventsPublished); Unit (Go) tests
issues.detail: With `SystemModstamp >= watermark` and watermark = newest stamp published, the newest rows match again on every poll. An idle org re-sends its latest Closed Won deal every 2 minutes: about 720 a day, about 21.6K a month. Each costs an SQS send, receive and delete, a worker invocation and a DynamoDB transaction attempt. It also makes EventsPublished ('changes found per poll') and DuplicatesSkipped meaningless as signals. If a LIMIT is added to bound a Lambda run, and more rows than the LIMIT share one SystemModstamp (Data Loader or mass updates commit batches with one stamp), `>=` returns the same first rows every poll. The watermark then never advances: a livelock. REST queries return at most about 2,000 rows per batch, with done=false and a nextRecordsUrl, and the plan never says to follow it. Confidence: high (the 2,000-row batch comes from a search snippet of the official REST guide; the page returned 403). Sources: snippet of https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/resources-query.html
issues.suggestion: Preferred: the lagged half-open window from the commit-lag issue, which removes boundary republishing entirely. If you keep a data-driven watermark, store a composite keyset in SSM and query `WHERE (SystemModstamp > :ts OR (SystemModstamp = :ts AND Id > :id)) ORDER BY SystemModstamp, Id`. Either way, never use LIMIT or OFFSET, and always follow nextRecordsUrl until done=true. Add Go table-driven tests: an idle org publishes 0 messages; 2,500 rows share one stamp; a page boundary falls inside a tie.

issues.title: Partial publish failure can permanently skip a row
issues.plan_section: Happy path step 2 ('advances the watermark to the newest timestamp it published')
issues.detail: If row k fails to publish while rows k+1..n succeed, 'the newest timestamp it published' is past row k. Row k is then skipped until the nightly reconcile, and forever if it is an update. SendMessageBatch returns HTTP 200 (err == nil in the Go SDK) with a Failed list for per-entry failures. AWS says to check for batch errors even when the call returns 200. Code that only checks err loses messages silently. A Lambda timeout mid-publish is the same case. Confidence: high. Sources: snippet of https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_SendMessageBatch.html
issues.suggestion: Publish in (SystemModstamp, Id) order and stop at the first failure, whether that is an err or any Failed entry. Advance the watermark only through the last row of the unbroken run of successes; with the lagged-window design, advance to upper only when every row succeeded. Return an error so the run counts as failed. Re-publishing is safe because the write is idempotent. Unit-test with a fake SQS client that fails entry 3 of 10, and assert the new watermark equals entry 2's key.

issues.title: Partial batch responses must be switched on, and the 'worker crashes mid-batch' row describes the wrong behaviour
issues.plan_section: Failure handling rows 'Worker crashes mid-batch' and 'Bad data'; Happy path steps 3 and 6
issues.detail:
(a) Lambda uses the batchItemFailures list only when the event source mapping has FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures]; in SAM this goes under Events.<name>.Properties. Without it, a normal return counts as full success and SQS deletes every message, including ones marked failed. Every transient failure is then silently lost.
(b) The crash row claims a timeout or exception reports only the failed IDs. AWS: 'If your function throws an exception, the entire batch is considered a complete failure.' A timeout returns nothing at all. All 10 messages reappear after the visibility timeout and all 10 receive counts go up. One poison message that crashes the handler pushes 9 innocent messages toward the DLQ.
(c) Lambda also fails the whole batch if any itemIdentifier is empty, null, uses a bad key name, or names a message not in the batch.
(d) The queue visibility timeout must be at least the function timeout (Lambda checks this), and AWS recommends at least 6× the function timeout.
(e) Wording: SQS does not invoke Lambda. Lambda's pollers receive from SQS.
Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-errorhandling.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html ; snippet: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-property-function-sqs.html
issues.suggestion:
- Set FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures] in template.yaml, and add a test that parses the template and asserts it.
- Wrap each record in try/except so the handler never raises. Return {"batchItemFailures": [{"itemIdentifier": record['messageId']}]} for failures.
- Before running out of time (check context.get_remaining_time_in_millis()), mark unprocessed records as failed rather than timing out.
- Suggested timeouts: function 30 s, queue VisibilityTimeout 180 s.
- Rewrite the row: 'Exception or timeout → the whole batch is redelivered; already-written messages hit the version check and do nothing; the per-record try/except keeps one bad message from failing the batch.'
- For permanent errors: SendMessage to the DLQ first. If that succeeds, leave the record out of batchItemFailures and let Lambda delete it; don't call DeleteMessage yourself. If the DLQ send fails, report the record as failed.
- Powertools' BatchProcessor implements this pattern if you'd rather not hand-roll it.

issues.title: The DynamoDB transaction is under-specified: condition format, duplicate vs stale, invoice after an edit, customer upsert
issues.plan_section: Happy path step 5; Failure handling rows 'Duplicate message' and 'Out-of-order updates'; Observability metrics (DuplicatesSkipped, StaleVersionsDropped); Components (Mock ERP)
issues.detail:
- **Condition.** The order Put needs `attribute_not_exists(order_id) OR #ver < :ver`. Keeping the version as the SystemModstamp string relies on lexicographic order of one exact format. fake_salesforce/store.py emits `...000+0000`, while hand-written fixtures or the Python reconciler may emit `...Z`. '+' (0x2B) sorts before 'Z' (0x5A), so mixed formats silently compare wrong.
- **Duplicate vs stale.** A failed condition only says 'not newer'. To tell DuplicatesSkipped from StaleVersionsDropped, set ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure=ALL_OLD on the order Put. CancellationReasons[i] in the TransactionCanceledException then carries the existing item: equal version means duplicate, greater means stale. DynamoDB Local supports this from 1.25.0/2.2.0; LocalStack builds on DynamoDB Local, but verify it.
- **Invoice after an edit is undefined.** If the invoice Put uses attribute_not_exists, every real v2 update cancels the whole transaction with ConditionalCheckFailed on the invoice item. A worker that treats 'any ConditionalCheckFailed' as a duplicate then drops the update forever. If the Put is unconditional, an issued invoice's amount changes silently. The user's own sample 'deal edited twice' hits this.
- **Customer upsert.** It must be an Update with SET, because a Put wipes fields. It is last-writer-wins across different deals of the same Account: an older message for deal A can overwrite the newer Account.Name that deal B brought. Two concurrent transactions touching one customer item fail with TransactionConflict, which must count as transient.
- **One item per action.** No two actions in a transaction may target the same item.
Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_TransactWriteItems.html ; snippet: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/12/amazon-dynamodb-local-two-api-features ; local file fake_salesforce/store.py
issues.suggestion:
- Store the version as a Number (epoch milliseconds of SystemModstamp).
- Invoice: I suggest 'the invoice mirrors the latest order'. INV-<OppId> carries the same source_version and the same version condition, plus a revision counter. The alternative, an immutable invoice with later edits reported as drift, is a larger design change. Choose one explicitly and write it into PLAN.md.
- Customer: Update with `SET #name=:n, account_version=:av`, conditioned on `attribute_not_exists(customer_id) OR account_version <= :av` using Account.SystemModstamp. Or state plainly that it is last-writer-wins.
- Map CancellationReasons by index (order, customer, invoice). Only ConditionalCheckFailed on the order item means duplicate or stale.
- Tests: replay v1→v2→v1; v2 after the invoice exists; two deals of one Account written concurrently; duplicate vs stale metric emission.
- Note that transactional writes consume double write capacity. This is from DynamoDB docs and was not re-checked this session.

issues.title: Transient vs permanent needs concrete rules; the visibility-timeout backoff and retry budget are unstated
issues.plan_section: Failure handling (ERP unavailable, Bad data, the 'Transient vs permanent' paragraph); Testing strategy (backoff calculation, the 100%-failure test); Interview question 6
issues.detail:
- TransactionCanceledException carries four different meanings. ConditionalCheckFailed on the order item means success (ack it and emit the metric). TransactionConflict, ThrottlingError and ProvisionedThroughputExceeded are transient. ValidationError is a code bug. Classifying by exception name alone misroutes them.
- Unknown exceptions (a KeyError from a mapping bug, a timeout reading SSM) need a default. Defaulting to permanent dead-letters good data after a bad deploy; defaulting to transient is bounded by maxReceiveCount anyway.
- The attempt number must come from the record's attributes.ApproximateReceiveCount. The worker must call ChangeMessageVisibility(receiptHandle, min(cap, base·2^(n−1) + jitter)) before returning the failure. It needs sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility permission and must stay under SQS's 12-hour maximum. AWS's docs say failed messages reappear 'after your queue's visibility timeout runs out', so Lambda does not reset it and the worker's value should hold. The local pump cannot prove that; one AWS check can.
- No numbers are given. With 5 receives and a 30 s base, the whole budget is about 7.5 minutes, so the '2-hour ERP outage' in interview question 6 dead-letters everything.
- With maxReceiveCount above 3, SQS moves messages received 3 or more times to the back of the queue, and ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage then reports the next message. The 'worker is stuck' alarm misses poison messages yet fires during legitimate backoff over 10 minutes.
- The 100%-failure test waits the full backoff unless the base is configurable.
Confidence: high; medium-high on Lambda not resetting visibility. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_TransactWriteItems.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-errorhandling.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html
issues.suggestion:
- Add a classification table to PLAN.md:
  - ConditionalCheckFailed on the order → ack, plus the duplicate or stale metric.
  - Transient → retry: TransactionConflict, ThrottlingError, ProvisionedThroughputExceeded, the chaos throttle, 5xx, timeouts and unknown exceptions.
  - Permanent → DLQ with a reason attribute: missing Amount or Account, unmappable fields, ValidationError.
- Make BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS (1 locally, 60 on AWS) and BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS (900) environment settings. With maxReceiveCount 5 that gives about a 15-minute budget.
- Write down the interview question 6 answer: longer outages land in the DLQ and are recovered by `relayctl dlq redrive` or the nightly reconciler.
- Set the age alarm above the backoff budget.
- Unit-test each mapping with botocore's Stubber returning CancellationReasons payloads.
- Add one deployed check that a transient failure reappears only after the backoff delay.

issues.title: CI/CD: the OIDC role must exist before CI can create it; deploy wiring has gaps
issues.plan_section: CI/CD (diagram; Deploy and Smoke rows; Authentication; Rollback); 2-day build plan 2.1/2.2
issues.detail:
- The GitHub OIDC provider and the deploy role must exist before the first workflow can assume them, so they cannot live only in the stack CI deploys. Put them in template.yaml and the role updates itself mid-deploy; one bad change locks CI out.
- GitHub's token subject is `repo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/heads/main` only if the job does not reference an environment. With `environment: dev` it becomes `repo:ORG/REPO:environment:dev`, and a trust policy keyed on the branch rejects it.
- The workflow needs `permissions: id-token: write`.
- 'Push to ECR → sam deploy' duplicates work: for image functions, `sam deploy` pushes what `sam build` built. The SHA tag you push yourself is not what the function references, so 'redeploy the previous SHA' is really 're-run the old commit's workflow' or 'git revert'.
- If you build and push with buildx or docker/build-push-action, Lambda requires --provenance=false and a single platform; Lambda does not support multi-architecture images.
- The diagram runs Integration before Build, but integration needs the images.
- CI also needs the LocalStack CI token.
- A failed first create leaves the stack in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, and deploys keep failing until `sam delete`.
Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/sam-cli-command-reference-sam-pipeline-bootstrap.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/go-image.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html
issues.suggestion:
- Add a one-time bootstrap, run by the user from the laptop with approval: `sam pipeline bootstrap --stage dev --permissions-provider oidc --oidc-provider github-actions --oidc-provider-url https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com --oidc-client-id sts.amazonaws.com --github-org <owner> --github-repo <repo> --deployment-branch main --create-image-repository`.
  - It creates the pipeline role, the CloudFormation execution role, the artifacts bucket and the ECR repo in their own stack.
  - This is a deliberate, stated exception to 'one stack': it is the same IaC tool and not a second environment.
- Keep the non-secret outputs in samconfig.toml or GitHub Variables.
- Deploy job:
  - no `environment:` key (or trust the environment subject);
  - aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials with role-to-assume;
  - `sam build`;
  - `sam deploy --no-confirm-changeset --no-fail-on-empty-changeset --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM --image-repository <uri> --s3-bucket <bucket>`.
- Drop the separate 'Push to ECR' stage and let compose build the images before integration.
- Rollback = git revert.
- Do the first deploy from the laptop in Phase 2.1 with the same stack name.
- Give the pipeline role only the extra data access the smoke test needs.
- PR workflows never assume the AWS role.

issues.title: The repo sits in a OneDrive-synced folder whose name contains a space
issues.plan_section: Not covered in PLAN.md; CLAUDE.md 'Stack and layout' and the autonomous-commit rule; the environment
issues.detail:
The repo is at C:\Users\luckf\OneDrive\Desktop\EverPure Relay (it has its own .git; I checked).
1. OneDrive syncing .git while git rewrites index and pack files is a widely reported corruption source, along with '-DESKTOP-xxxx' conflict copies. Files On-Demand can turn files into cloud-only placeholders that Docker build contexts and tests trip over.
2. .gitignore does not stop OneDrive, so .env (Salesforce secret, LocalStack token) is uploaded to Microsoft's cloud.
3. Docker's WSL2 guidance: bind mounts from the Windows filesystem are much slower, and 'Linux containers only receive file change events ... if the original files are stored in the Linux filesystem'.
4. The space breaks unquoted $(pwd) or $PWD in scripts, make, and unquoted compose volume strings.
5. .aws-sam/, .venv and caches churn through sync and can lock files during `sam build`.
Confidence: high for Docker/WSL (official doc); medium for OneDrive corruption (community reports). Sources read: https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/wsl/best-practices/ ; snippet: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/discussions/onedriveforbusiness/onedrive-is-corrupting-my-git-repositories/3898283
issues.suggestion: Before more commits, move the repo out of OneDrive to a path with no spaces. Best is inside WSL2 (e.g. ~/code/relay), running docker, sam, go and pytest from WSL. Acceptable is C:\dev\relay. Moving the folder keeps .git intact. If the user insists on staying in OneDrive, pause sync for the folder and keep .env outside the synced tree. Keep the existing .gitattributes (`* text=auto eol=lf`), which is correct.

issues.title: The reconciler checks only missing orders, and re-enqueues deals that can never succeed
issues.plan_section: Components (Reconciler); Failure handling rows 'Poller misses a record' and 'Deal deleted or reverted'; Testing (Reconciliation); Observability (DriftFound); 2.3 'Done when'
issues.detail:
- Only 'Closed Won deals with no matching order' are compared. Missed updates from commit lag or same-second ties leave an order at an old version forever, and they are never flagged.
- It re-enqueues every Closed Won deal without an order. That includes the 'no Amount' sample deal the user is told to create, which fails validation again. So every night: DLQ, DLQ alarm, human noise, and the alarm never returns to OK.
- Deleted opportunities are not returned by a normal SOQL query (queryAll or IsDeleted is needed), so 'deleted' and 'reverted' cannot be told apart.
- The Python reconciler re-implements OAuth, SOQL and the message schema that the Go poller owns. Drift between the two implementations becomes a new failure mode.
- It will flag the CI smoke-test order as drift every night (see smoke issue).
Confidence: high (design analysis).
issues.suggestion:
Compare per OpportunityId:
(a) Salesforce Closed Won and no order → re-enqueue only if the shared validate() passes; otherwise report 'invalid in source'.
(b) The order's version or content hash is behind Salesforce → re-enqueue it as a missed update.
(c) An order exists but Salesforce is no longer IsWon, or the deal is deleted (queryAll, IsDeleted) → report only.
(d) Skip SMOKE- IDs.
Keep one JSON Schema for the message (e.g. schemas/opportunity_event.json) and validate against it in both Go and Python tests. Or have the reconciler invoke the ingest Lambda with {"ids": [...]} so only Go ever builds messages. Change the reconciliation test to cover (a)–(c).

issues.title: The smoke test can pass without testing anything, and it pollutes the ERP
issues.plan_section: CI/CD (Smoke row); Testing strategy (Smoke)
issues.detail: A synthetic message with a fixed OpportunityId passes from the second run onward, because the order from run 1 already exists and the new message is dropped as a duplicate. The test then proves nothing about the pipeline. The synthetic order has no Salesforce counterpart, so the reconciler reports it as drift every night. It also appears in demos and in the reconciler's 'repaired' counts. The CI role needs SQS and DynamoDB data permissions the plan doesn't mention. Confidence: high (design analysis).
issues.suggestion: Use a unique ID and version per run (e.g. 006SMOKE<sha8><attempt>). Assert that both the order and the invoice appear within 60 s. Then delete the three items, or give them a TTL attribute with DynamoDB TTL enabled (TTL deletion is asynchronous). The reconciler ignores the SMOKE prefix. Grant the pipeline role only sqs:SendMessage on the main queue plus dynamodb:GetItem and DeleteItem on the three tables.

issues.title: Poller runs can overlap (Scheduler invokes asynchronously and Lambda retries), and the ingest alarm is mis-set
issues.plan_section: Components (Ingest poller, EventBridge Scheduler every 2 min); Observability ('ingest Lambda errors > 0 for 3 runs in a row')
issues.detail: EventBridge Scheduler invokes Lambda asynchronously. On a function error Lambda retries twice, after 1 minute and then 2 minutes, so a failing 2-minute poller overlaps its own next scheduled runs. Two pollers can publish the same window, and the slower one can write an older watermark back to SSM. That rewinds the watermark and triggers noisy republishes. One bad tick yields about 3 errors in about 3 minutes, so the '3 runs in a row' alarm fires on a single failure. With a 2-minute schedule and 1-minute Lambda metrics, every other datapoint is missing, which breaks naive 'N consecutive periods' alarms. Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-eventbridge-scheduler.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async-error-handling.html
issues.suggestion:
In template.yaml:
- Poller ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 1.
- EventInvokeConfig: MaximumRetryAttempts 0 and MaximumEventAgeInSeconds 60, so the next tick is the retry.
- ScheduleV2: RetryPolicy MaximumRetryAttempts 0, and State driven by a parameter, which is the pause flag.
Only write the watermark forward: read, compare, write, which is safe with concurrency 1. Alarm on Errors Sum ≥ 3 with Period 600, 1 evaluation period and TreatMissingData notBreaching. Alternatively, alarm when a custom PollSucceeded metric is missing for 10 minutes. The Go handler must return an error on Salesforce auth failure, not log it and return nil.

issues.title: Salesforce timestamps have one-second precision, so two edits in the same second share a version
issues.plan_section: Happy path step 2 (event key) and step 5 (version); Failure handling 'Out-of-order updates'
issues.detail: Salesforce datetime fields do not store milliseconds; SOQL always returns .000. fake_salesforce/store.py deliberately stamps to the second. Two edits of the same deal within one second produce the same event key and version: a user save followed immediately by a flow or trigger field update, or a script. Under the strict `<` condition, the second, different content is classified as a duplicate and dropped. The ERP keeps stale data until the next edit, and no metric reveals it. Confidence: medium-high. The official page could not be fetched; the finding rests on search snippets and on the local fake store's own assumption. Sources: snippet of https://ideas.salesforce.com/s/idea/a0B8W00000GdWyhUAF/millisecond-precision-in-datetime-fields and https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=001118432&language=en_US&type=1 ; local file fake_salesforce/store.py
issues.suggestion: Add a content hash (sha256 of the mapped fields) to the message and the order item. Use the condition `attribute_not_exists(order_id) OR #ver < :ver OR (#ver = :ver AND #hash <> :hash)` and count the equal-version path as an update. Put an 8-character hash in the logged event key (OppId:modstamp:hash8). The reconciler compares hashes. Unit test: two payloads with the same stamp and different Amounts.

issues.title: The exactly-once claim promises more than the design delivers
issues.plan_section: Intro paragraph; 'The core idea to explain in interviews'; Resume bullets
issues.detail:
Idempotent, version-guarded upserts give 'at most one order per deal, converging to the newest version seen'. That is exactly-once effect on state, not per event. The intro promises every Closed Won deal mirrored exactly once 'even when ... the ERP is down'. But:
- Invalid deals are dead-lettered by design and never mirrored.
- ERP outages longer than the retry budget land in the DLQ until a redrive or the nightly reconcile.
- Same-second ties, misclassified cancellations and commit-lag misses (issues above) break convergence.
- Effects outside DynamoDB are at-least-once. EMF metrics can count OrdersWritten on attempt 1 and DuplicatesSkipped on attempt 2. A permanent-error message can land in the DLQ twice if Lambda dies after the send.
The plan is right that no outbox table is needed. Confidence: high (design analysis).
issues.suggestion: Reword the intro, interview line and resume bullet to: 'At-least-once delivery plus idempotent, version-guarded writes: each Closed Won deal yields at most one order and one invoice, which converge to the latest Salesforce version. Invalid deals are dead-lettered with a reason, and the nightly reconciler finds anything missed.' Note in Observability that metrics are approximate under retries.

issues.title: CloudFormation can't create the SecureString secret, and runtime-written parameters shouldn't be stack-owned
issues.plan_section: Components (Config and secrets in SSM Parameter Store; Infrastructure = SAM); CLAUDE.md (where to put credentials)
issues.detail: AWS::SSM::Parameter allows only String and StringList: 'Parameters of type SecureString are not supported by AWS CloudFormation.' So the Salesforce client secret must be created outside the stack, and the plan never says who does it or when. Creating it with `aws ssm put-parameter --value <secret>` leaves the secret in PowerShell's PSReadLine history file. The poller writes the watermark and relayctl writes the chaos flags at runtime. If template.yaml owns them, a later change to their Value resets the watermark (a full republish) or the chaos rate, and `sam delete` removes them. Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ssm-parameter.html
issues.suggestion: Add a manual step for the user, with approval: Systems Manager console > Parameter Store > Create parameter. Name /relay/dev/salesforce/client_secret, Tier Standard, Type SecureString, KMS key alias/aws/ssm. The client ID and My Domain URL can be String parameters owned by the template. Lambdas read the secret with GetParameter(WithDecryption=True) once per cold start and cache it; the role needs ssm:GetParameter on those ARNs. Don't declare /relay/dev/watermark in the template. The poller treats ParameterNotFound as 'start from a configured date' and creates the parameter with Overwrite. relayctl creates the chaos flags, defaulting to 0. Locally, a LocalStack ready.d init script seeds the same names.

issues.title: ECR storage grows with every merge, and a careless cleanup rule breaks the live function
issues.plan_section: AWS cost (ECR row); CI/CD (Push to ECR, Rollback)
issues.detail: Every merge to main pushes 3 new images and nothing deletes them. With --resolve-image-repos, SAM creates one repository per function in a companion stack. Layers are de-duplicated only within a repository, so the worker and reconciler each store the full Python base image. On the new Free account plan only Always Free offers are active; ECR's '500 MB for one year' is a new-customer trial. Storage therefore draws on credits or is billed at $0.10 per GB-month. An age-only lifecycle rule can delete the image the live function uses. AWS: if the image 'no longer exists ... the function enters the Failed state'. Confidence: high; medium on how ECR's trial applies to Free-plan accounts. Sources read: https://aws.amazon.com/ecr/pricing/ , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/free-tier.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html
issues.suggestion: Use one repository you own, created by the bootstrap stack or `sam pipeline bootstrap --create-image-repository`, and pass it with --image-repository. Give it a lifecycle policy: rule 1 expires untagged images after 1 day; rule 2 keeps the newest 10 images (imageCountMoreThan). Never use an age-only rule. Optionally ship the worker and reconciler as one Python image with two handlers (ImageConfig.Command) to halve storage and build time.

issues.title: Alarms have no delivery path; email subscriptions need confirmation within 48 hours
issues.plan_section: Observability (Alarms); 2.3 'Done when: the DLQ alarm fires'
issues.detail: Three alarms are defined but no SNS topic or alarm actions, so 'a human must look' reaches nobody. An email subscription created by CloudFormation sits in PendingConfirmation until the link is clicked. SNS 'deletes all other unconfirmed subscriptions after 48 hours', while the stack still shows the subscription resource as created. A missed or spam-filtered email therefore means silent alarms. Hard-coding the address in template.yaml or a committed samconfig.toml puts personal data in a likely public repo. The age and ingest alarm thresholds also need fixing (see the classification and poller-overlap issues). Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-email-notifications.html
issues.suggestion: Add an AlertTopic (AWS::SNS::Topic) and an AWS::SNS::Subscription with Protocol email and Endpoint from an AlertEmail parameter. Put AlarmActions and OKActions on every alarm. Pass AlertEmail from a GitHub Actions Variable and from samconfig.local.toml, which is already gitignored. Checklist item: 'Click Confirm subscription within 48 hours; check spam.' Test with `aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --state-value ALARM` (needs approval). DLQ alarm: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, Maximum > 0, Period 60, TreatMissingData notBreaching.

issues.title: DLQ details: retention, direct sends, the redrive API, and an alarm that stays red
issues.plan_section: Failure handling ('ERP unavailable', 'Bad data'); Components (relayctl DLQ inspect and redrive)
issues.detail:
- **Retention.** For standard queues 'the enqueue timestamp is unchanged' when a message moves to the DLQ. With the default 4-day retention, a message can expire from the DLQ early; AWS says to set DLQ retention longer than the source queue's.
- **Redrive API.** StartMessageMoveTask accepts only DLQs whose sources are SQS queues. Without DestinationArn, it moves messages back 'to their respective original source queues'. Messages the worker sent directly (permanent errors) should be redriven with an explicit DestinationArn. Only one move task per queue can run at a time.
- **Redriving permanent errors** just dead-letters them again. Bad data is fixed by editing Salesforce, which produces a new version.
- **The alarm stays red.** The user's own 'no Amount' sample puts DLQ depth above 0 from the first deploy, so the alarm is permanently in ALARM.
Confidence: high. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_StartMessageMoveTask.html
issues.suggestion:
Set the DLQ MessageRetentionPeriod to 1209600 (14 days); the source queue can stay at 4 days. relayctl commands:
- `dlq list`: peek with VisibilityTimeout 0 and show the reason attribute and receive count.
- `dlq redrive --transient-only`: receive, filter on reason, send, delete; or StartMessageMoveTask with an explicit DestinationArn.
- `dlq ack <id>`: delete a triaged message.
Document the runbook: fix in Salesforce → the new version flows → ack the old DLQ entry.

issues.title: Parts of the cost section are out of date or off by an order of magnitude
issues.plan_section: AWS cost (table, source link, 'nothing runs (or costs) when idle')
issues.detail:
(1) The source is a third-party aggregator (agentdeals.dev), not AWS.
(2) Accounts created on or after 15 July 2025 get $100 in credits, plus up to $100 more for activities. The Free account plan ends after 6 months or when credits run out, whichever is first. It has only Always Free offers active and blocks some services. The plan should say which account plan the user is on.
(3) SQS: 'a few tens of thousands' is too low, and 'nothing runs when idle' is false. Lambda keeps long-polling an idle queue. In standard mode it scales down to 'as few as 2 concurrent invokes'. Setting MaximumConcurrency disables that optimisation, leaving 5. At one 20-second poll per poller that is about 0.26M–0.65M ReceiveMessage calls a month (my own arithmetic from the AWS figures), plus about 22K republished boundary messages. That is still under the 1M Always Free requests.
(4) DynamoDB: the 25 WCU / 25 RCU Always Free applies to provisioned capacity; on-demand is billed per request. Transactions double write consumption, so 5 WCU per table can throttle under a 10-message burst.
(5) CloudWatch free tier: 10 custom metrics, 10 standard-resolution alarm metrics, 3 dashboards of 50 metrics, 5 GB of logs. Each EMF metric name × dimension set counts separately, so extra dimensions quickly exceed 10, at $0.30 per metric-month.
(6) LocalStack now needs an account.
Confidence: high; the idle-poll count is derived. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/free-tier.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html , https://aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/pricing/ , https://aws.amazon.com/ecr/pricing/
issues.suggestion: Cite aws.amazon.com/free and the service pricing pages instead of the aggregator. Change the SQS row to 'about 0.3–0.7M requests a month, within the 1M free tier', and drop 'nothing runs when idle'. Choose DynamoDB on-demand explicitly, or provisioned capacity with throttles classified as transient. Fix one EMF dimension set (e.g. Service=relay) to stay under 10 metrics. Add a line on Free vs Paid account plans. If the worker needs a concurrency cap to protect the ERP, use ScalingConfig.MaximumConcurrency (minimum 2) rather than reserved concurrency, and note that it keeps 5 pollers when idle.

issues.title: The $1 AWS Budget may never fire while credits cover the spend
issues.plan_section: AWS cost ('Do on day 1'); 1.1 (You: $1 AWS Budget alert)
issues.detail: A cost budget measured after credits (the 'net' cost options) stays at $0 while the $100–$200 of credits absorb charges. A runaway NAT gateway then consumes credits with no alert. AWS's own guidance for credit-funded accounts: 'make sure the credits options is not checked, otherwise you won't track the costs if paying with credits.' Budget data is also refreshed only a few times a day, so it is a lagging signal, not a guardrail. Confidence: medium; the console wording has changed from a 'Credits' checkbox to cost-aggregation choices. Sources read: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-cost-budget.html , https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/startups/how-to-set-aws-budget-when-paying-with-aws-credits/
issues.suggestion: Checklist steps: Billing and Cost Management > Budgets > Create budget > Customize (advanced) > Cost budget > Period Monthly, Recurring, Fixed, $1. Under Advanced options choose 'Use unblended costs', not the 'net' options; if the console offers charge-type options, exclude Credits and Refunds. Add alerts at 100% Actual and 100% Forecasted to the user's email. Keep the cost-avoidance rules (no NAT, VPC or hourly services), which are the real protection.

issues.title: Local AWS setup contradicts 'no long-lived keys', and the guardrails miss SDK-driven calls
issues.plan_section: CLAUDE.md (Hard rules; 'Stop and ask'; 'Tests must never need a real AWS account'); .claude/settings.json
issues.detail:
- The user is asked to 'configure the AWS CLI locally'. `aws configure` stores long-lived access keys, which CLAUDE.md forbids ('No long-lived AWS keys anywhere').
- Once a default profile exists, any SDK code run locally reaches the real account if an endpoint override is missing: pytest, go run, relayctl.
- settings.json allows all Bash, and the only guard is `Bash(aws:*)`. That does not catch `python -c ...`, `pytest`, `go run ./relayctl`, or `docker push` to ECR. Nor does it catch `sam pipeline bootstrap`, which creates IAM roles, the OIDC provider, S3 and ECR, or `sam remote invoke`.
- On Windows, Claude Code's PowerShell tool is governed by PowerShell(...) rules, not Bash(...) rules. PowerShell commands still prompt, because PowerShell isn't allow-listed, but the rule set is inconsistent.
- Ask rules take precedence over allow rules, so a broad Bash(sam:*) ask would also prompt for `sam build`.
Confidence: high on permissions (docs); medium on the `aws login` version (AWS announcement snippet). Sources read: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions , https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings ; snippet: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/11/console-credentials-aws-cli-sdk-authentication/

issues.title: Salesforce details the checklist and poller need: My Domain token URL, run-as user, org expiry, datetime literals
issues.plan_section: Components ('Salesforce side'); Happy path step 1; Testing (Contract); 1.1
issues.detail:
(1) Client credentials requests to login.salesforce.com or test.salesforce.com are not supported. The token endpoint must be the org's My Domain URL, https://<mydomain>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token.
(2) The flow needs a Run As (execution) user. Tokens act as that user, who needs API Enabled plus read access to Opportunity and Account.
(3) Developer Edition orgs not logged into for 45 days are deleted (legacy DE orgs: 180 days). It is unclear whether client-credentials API logins count, so the org could disappear after the project.
(4) SOQL datetime literals are unquoted ISO-8601. A '+' offset must be URL-encoded as %2B or it becomes a space, so use the Z form and encode the whole q parameter.
(5) `StageName = 'Closed Won'` depends on an editable picklist label. `IsWon = true` is the stable field, and the fake stub already supports it.
(6) The API version is not pinned.
(7) The recorded real response for the contract test will contain the My Domain host and real IDs and names.
Confidence: medium. Salesforce pages returned 403 to my fetcher; these points come from search snippets of the official pages. Sources (snippets): https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=xcloud.remoteaccess_oauth_client_credentials_flow.htm&type=5 , https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.admin_de_org_expiration.htm&language=en_US&type=5 , https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-valid-date-formats.html
issues.suggestion: .env values: SF_LOGIN_URL=https://<mydomain>.my.salesforce.com, SF_CLIENT_ID, SF_CLIENT_SECRET, and SF_API_VERSION pinned to a version listed at /services/data/. No username or password. Use `IsWon = true` in the poller and reconciler SOQL. Scrub the host, IDs and names from the recorded contract fixture before committing. Checklist: log into the org in a browser at least monthly.

issues.title: The 'why polling' rationale ignores Salesforce Event Relay
issues.plan_section: Architecture ('Why polling instead of push?'); What not to build (Pub/Sub API); Interview question 7
issues.detail: Change Data Capture is not only a long-lived gRPC/Avro stream. Salesforce Event Relay (generally available since 2022) delivers CDC and platform events to an Amazon EventBridge partner event bus as a managed subscription, with no long-lived connection in Lambda. 'Fights Lambda's short-lived model' is true for Pub/Sub API clients, but an interviewer who knows Event Relay will challenge it. Polling is still a fine teaching choice. Confidence: medium; I did not verify Event Relay's availability in Developer Edition. Sources (snippet): https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2022/10/salesforce-event-relay-is-generally-available
issues.suggestion: Keep polling, and reword the rationale: 'Polling is simple, cheap and teaches the watermark problem. The push alternative is CDC → Event Relay → EventBridge → SQS, which removes the watermark but adds replay, ordering and gap-event handling.' Use this as the interview question 7 answer.

issues.title: Windows and tooling trip-wires
issues.plan_section: CLAUDE.md 'Stack and layout' (python3 --version; golangci-lint); Docker (images); Infrastructure (log retention)
issues.detail:
- On Windows, `python3 --version` often hits the Microsoft Store app-execution alias instead of the real interpreter. From general knowledge; not verified this session.
- golangci-lint v2 (March 2025) requires a `version: "2"` config. v1 configs, and many tutorials, fail; `golangci-lint migrate` converts them.
- Images built with buildx need --provenance=false and a single --platform that matches Architectures in template.yaml.
- boto3's DynamoDB serializer rejects Python float, and the fake stub emits Amount as a float. Well-known boto3 behaviour; not re-verified.
- Lambda auto-creates /aws/lambda/<fn> with never-expire retention on first invoke. If the stack declares that log group and the function runs first (the SQS mapping starts immediately), stack creation can fail with 'already exists'.
Confidence: mixed, as marked. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/go-image.html (read); snippets: https://golangci-lint.run/docs/product/migration-guide/ , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-lambda-function-loggingconfig.html
issues.suggestion:
- Check the interpreter with `py -3 --version` or `python --version`.
- Write .golangci.yml in v2 format.
- Add `--provenance=false --platform linux/amd64` wherever buildx is used.
- Parse SQS bodies with `json.loads(body, parse_float=Decimal)`.
- Declare each log group as AWS::Logs::LogGroup with RetentionInDays 7, a name without the 'aws/' prefix, and point the function's LoggingConfig.LogGroup at it.
